title.en: Volume 62 Biographies 52: He Yang, Sima Jiong, Zhu Yi, Gu Xie, Xu Chi, Bao Quan
title.raw: 卷六十二 列傳第五十二 賀瑒 司馬褧 朱异 顧協 徐摛 鮑泉 Volume 62 Biographies 52: He Yang, Sima Jiong, Zhu Yi, Gu Xie, Xu Chi, Bao Quan

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十二

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 52
translations.idiomatic: Biography 52

sentences.zh: 賀瑒司馬褧朱異顧協徐摛鮑泉

translations.literal: He Yang, Sima Jiong, Zhu Yi, Gu Xie, Xu Chi, Bao Quan
translations.idiomatic: He Yang, Sima Jiong, Zhu Yi, Gu Xie, Xu Chi, and Bao Quan

sentences.zh: 瑒少聰敏，齊時沛國劉瓛為會稽府丞，見瑒深器異之。

translations.literal: Yang was clever from youth. During Qi, Liu Huan of Pei was assistant administrator of Kuaiji prefecture; seeing Yang, he greatly valued and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He Yang was bright even as a boy. In the Qi period, Liu Huan of Pei served as assistant administrator in Kuaiji and, on meeting Yang, took a deep liking to him and saw unusual promise in him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與俱造吳郡張融，指瑒謂曰：「此生將來為儒者宗矣。

translations.literal: Once he went with him to visit Zhang Rong of Wu commandery, pointed at Yang and said: "This youth will in future be the leader of the Confucians."
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he took Yang to call on Zhang Rong of Wu commandery, pointed to the boy, and said, "This lad will one day be a master among the Ru scholars."

sentences.zh: 」薦之為國子生，舉明經。

translations.literal: " He recommended him as a student of the Imperial University and had him nominated for mastery of the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: " He recommended Yang for enrollment as a national university student and had him nominated in the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 後為太學博士。

translations.literal: Later he became an Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as an Erudite at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，為太常丞，有司舉修賓禮，召見說禮義。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian of Liang, he was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the relevant offices recommended him to revise the guest rites, and he was summoned for an audience to expound ritual meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang emperor Wu's Tianjian era, he served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. When the authorities nominated him to revise the rites for receiving guests, he was summoned to court to explain ritual principles.

sentences.zh: 武帝異之，詔朝朔望，預華林講。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu regarded him as extraordinary and ordered him to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month, participating in the Huilin lectures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and commanded him to attend court on the new and full moon of each month and to take part in the Huilin lecture series.

sentences.zh: 四年，初開五館，以瑒兼五經博士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the Five Halls were first opened, Yang was made concurrent Erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the Five Halls were first established, Yang was appointed concurrent Erudite for the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 別詔為皇太子定禮，撰五經義。

translations.literal: By separate edict he was charged to fix ritual for the Crown Prince and to compile exegeses of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: A separate edict assigned him to set down ritual for the crown prince and to compile commentaries on the meaning of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 時武帝方創定禮樂，瑒所建議多見施行。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu was just establishing rites and music; many of Yang's proposals were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was still creating the new ritual and music code, most of Yang's recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜步兵校尉，領五經博士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and continued as Erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he received the post of Commandant of Footsoldiers while retaining his charge as Erudite of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 卒於館。

translations.literal: He died at the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the academy hall.

sentences.zh: 所著禮、易、老、莊講疏，朝廷博士議數百篇，賓禮儀注一百四十五卷。

translations.literal: His writings included lecture commentaries on the Rites, Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, several hundred memorial discussions as Court Erudite, and 145 juan of annotated guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote lecture commentaries on the Rites, the Changes, the Laozi, and the Zhuangzi, several hundred policy memorials from his tenure as court erudite, and a 145-juan commentary on guest ritual.

sentences.zh: 瑒于禮尤精，館中生徒常數百，弟子明經對策至數十人。

translations.literal: Yang was especially expert in the Rites; students in the Hall often numbered in the hundreds, and disciples who passed the Mingjing examination and policy response reached several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was preeminent in ritual studies. His hall regularly held several hundred pupils, and dozens of his students passed the classics examination and policy tests.

sentences.zh: 二子革、季，弟子琛，並傳瑒業。

translations.literal: His two sons Ge and Ji, and his disciple Chen, all transmitted Yang's learning.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Ge and Ji and his disciple Chen all carried on his scholarly tradition.

sentences.zh: 革字文明，少以家貧，躬耕供養，年二十，始輟耒就父受業，精力不怠。

translations.literal: Ge, style name Wenming, in youth because the family was poor personally plowed the fields to provide support; at age twenty he first laid aside the plough to study under his father, his energy never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Ge, whose style was Wenming, grew up in poverty and farmed with his own hands to support the household. Only at twenty did he set aside the plough to study under his father, and he never flagged in his diligence.

sentences.zh: 有六尺方床，思義未達，則橫臥其上，不盡其義，終不肯食。

translations.literal: He had a six-foot square couch; when the meaning of a passage had not been grasped he would lie across it, and until he had fully understood the meaning he would in the end refuse to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a six-foot square couch. Whenever a passage's meaning eluded him, he would stretch out on it and refuse to eat until he had worked the sense through completely.

sentences.zh: 通三禮。

translations.literal: He mastered the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He attained mastery of the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 及長，遍治孝經、論語、毛詩、左傳，為兼太學博士。

translations.literal: When grown, he thoroughly studied the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, and Zuo Commentary, and became concurrent Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he studied the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao version of the Odes, and the Zuo Commentary in full, and was appointed concurrent Erudite at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 長七尺八寸，雍容都雅，吐納蘊藉。

translations.literal: He was seven chi eight cun in height, dignified and refined in bearing, restrained and elegant in speech.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi eight cun tall, carried himself with dignified grace, and spoke with quiet, cultivated restraint.

sentences.zh: 敕于永福省為邵陵、湘東、武陵三王講禮。

translations.literal: By imperial order at Yongfu Palace he lectured on ritual for the Princes of Shaoling, Xiangdong, and Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he taught ritual at Yongfu Palace to the princes of Shaoling, Xiangdong, and Wuling.

sentences.zh: 後為國子博士，于學講授，生徒常數百人。

translations.literal: Later he became Erudite of the National University; lecturing at the school, his students often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Erudite of the National University, where he lectured to audiences that regularly numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 出為西中郎湘東王諮議參軍，帶江陵令。

translations.literal: He went out as Staff Adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Western Gentlemen of the Palace, and concurrently served as magistrate of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as staff adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong, Western Palace Gentleman-General, while also holding the post of magistrate of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 王於州置學，以革領儒林祭酒，講三禮，荊楚衣冠聽者甚眾。

translations.literal: The prince established a school in the province and made Ge head Libationer of the Confucian Grove; lecturing on the Three Rites, very many gentry of Jing and Chu came to listen.
translations.idiomatic: The prince founded a provincial school and appointed Ge Libationer of the Confucian Grove. When he lectured on the Three Rites, the leading families of Jing and Chu turned out in great numbers to hear him.

sentences.zh: 前後再監南平郡，為人吏所懷。

translations.literal: Before and after he twice supervised Nanping commandery and was cherished by the people and officials.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as supervisor of Nanping commandery, and both the populace and the officials held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 尋兼平西長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West and Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added the posts of chief clerk for the Pacification of the West and administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 革至孝，常恨食祿代耕，不及為養。

translations.literal: Ge was extremely filial and often regretted that receiving salary in place of plowing did not allow him to provide support in person.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was profoundly filial and often lamented that drawing an official salary—'eating emolument in place of tilling'—kept him from supporting his parents himself.

sentences.zh: 在荊州曆為郡縣，所得俸秩，不及妻孥，專擬還鄉造寺，以申感思。

translations.literal: While in Jingzhou he successively held commandery and county posts; the salary he received did not reach wife and children—he intended solely to return home and build a temple to express grateful remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: During his years in Jingzhou he held a series of prefectural and county posts, but he never let his salary reach his wife and children. He planned to return home and build a temple as an act of filial gratitude.

sentences.zh: 子徽，美風儀，能談吐，深為革愛，先革卒。

translations.literal: His son Hui had fine bearing and could discourse well; Ge loved him deeply. Hui died before Ge.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui was handsome and eloquent and was dearly loved by Ge, but Hui died before his father.

sentences.zh: 革哭之，因遘疾而卒。

translations.literal: Ge wept for him and, encountering illness thereby, died.
translations.idiomatic: Ge mourned him so bitterly that he fell ill and soon died himself.

sentences.zh: 季亦明三禮，位中書黃門郎，兼著作。

translations.literal: Ji also understood the Three Rites and held the post of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat, concurrently Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was likewise versed in the Three Rites and rose to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat while also serving as a court compiler.

sentences.zh: 琛字國寶，幼孤，伯父瑒授其經業，一聞便通義理。

translations.literal: Chen, style name Guobao, was orphaned young; his uncle Yang taught him the classics, and upon one hearing he grasped the principles.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, style Guobao, lost his parents early. His uncle Yang trained him in the classics, and he understood their principles after a single hearing.

sentences.zh: 瑒異之，常曰：「此兒當以明經致貴。

translations.literal: Yang regarded him as extraordinary and often said: "This boy will attain eminence through mastery of the Classics."
translations.idiomatic: Yang marveled at him and often said, "This boy will win rank and honor through the classics examination."

sentences.zh: 」瑒卒後，琛家貧，常往還諸暨販粟以養母。

translations.literal: " After Yang died, Chen's family was poor; he often went back and forth to Zhuji to sell grain to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " After Yang's death the family fell on hard times, and Chen regularly traveled to Zhuji to trade grain so he could support his mother.

sentences.zh: 雖自執舟烜，閑則習業，尤精三禮。

translations.literal: Although he himself manned the boat and pole, in leisure he studied his craft and was especially expert in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Even while he poled his own boat on the river, he studied whenever he had a spare moment and became especially accomplished in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，瑒之門徒稍從問道。

translations.literal: When he was a little over twenty, Yang's disciples gradually came to him to inquire about the Way.
translations.idiomatic: By his mid-twenties, many of Yang's former students had begun coming to Chen for instruction.

sentences.zh: 初，瑒於鄉里聚徒教授，四方受業者三千餘人。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang had gathered disciples to teach in his home district; students who came from all directions numbered more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had once gathered pupils in his home district to teach, and more than three thousand students came from all quarters to study with him.

sentences.zh: 瑒天監中亡，至是復集，琛乃築室郊郭之際，茅茨數間，年將三十，便事講授。

translations.literal: Yang died in the Tianjian period; by this time they assembled again. Chen then built a dwelling on the outskirts of the city—a few thatched rooms—and when he was nearly thirty he undertook lecturing.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang died early in the Tianjian era, his students gradually reassembled. Chen built a few thatched rooms just outside the walls and, not yet thirty, began lecturing in earnest.

sentences.zh: 既世習禮學，究其精微，占述先儒，吐言辯絜，坐之聽受，終日不疲。

translations.literal: Having inherited ritual studies for generations, he plumbed their subtlety, cited and expounded the former Ru, his words clear and incisive; those seated to listen received instruction all day without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in ritual scholarship from childhood, he pursued its finest points, cited the early Confucians with precision, and spoke with luminous clarity. Listeners could sit before him all day without weariness.

sentences.zh: 湘東王幼年臨郡，彭城到溉為行事，聞琛美名，命駕相造。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong in youth governed the commandery; Dao Gai of Pengcheng was acting administrator. Hearing Chen's fine reputation, he ordered his carriage to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When the young Prince of Xiangdong took up his post in the commandery, Dao Gai of Pengcheng served as acting administrator. Hearing of Chen's renown, he had his carriage driven out to visit him.

sentences.zh: 會琛正講，學侶滿筵，既聞上佐忽來，莫不傾動。

translations.literal: It happened that Chen was lecturing and the hall was full of fellow students; when they heard the chief aide had suddenly arrived, none failed to be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was in the middle of a lecture, the benches packed with students, when word came that the chief administrator had arrived unexpectedly. The whole assembly stirred.

sentences.zh: 琛說經無輟，曾不降意。

translations.literal: Chen expounded the classics without pause and never lowered his manner.
translations.idiomatic: Chen never broke off his exposition and never showed the least deference.

sentences.zh: 溉下車，欣然就席，便申問難，往復從容，義理該贍。

translations.literal: Gai alighted from his carriage, gladly took a seat, and at once raised questions and objections; back and forth at ease, the principles were comprehensive and ample.
translations.idiomatic: Gai stepped down from his carriage, took a seat with evident pleasure, and entered into debate. Their exchange was unhurried, and Chen's reasoning proved complete and ample.

sentences.zh: 溉歎曰：「通儒碩學，復見賀生。

translations.literal: Gai sighed and said: "A penetrating Ru and great scholar—I see Master He again."
translations.idiomatic: Gai exclaimed, "A true master scholar—we have He Yang reborn!"

sentences.zh: 今且還城，尋當相屈。

translations.literal: For now I return to the city; soon I shall summon you.
translations.idiomatic: I must return to the city for now, but I shall call on you again before long."

sentences.zh: 」琛了不酬答，神用頹然。

translations.literal: " Chen made no reply at all, his spirit and manner utterly unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen offered no reply whatever, his bearing as composed as before.

sentences.zh: 溉言之王，請補郡功曹史。

translations.literal: Gai spoke of him to the prince and requested that he be appointed Commandery Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Gai reported to the prince and asked that Chen be appointed commandery merit officer.

sentences.zh: 琛辭以母老，終於固執。

translations.literal: Chen declined on the ground that his mother was old and in the end firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Chen declined on account of his aged mother and held firm to his refusal.

sentences.zh: 俄遭母憂，廬於墓所。

translations.literal: Soon he encountered mourning for his mother and built a hut at the grave site.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his mother died, and he built a mourning hut beside her tomb.

sentences.zh: 服闋，猶未還舍，生徒復從之。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he still had not returned home; students again followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he had still not moved back into his house, and his students gathered around him once more.

sentences.zh: 琛哀毀積年，骨立而已，未堪講授。

translations.literal: Chen's grief and emaciation accumulated for years until he was only bones standing; he was not yet able to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: For years Chen grieved until he was little more than a skeleton and was not yet fit to teach.

sentences.zh: 諸生營救，稍稍習業。

translations.literal: The students pressed him to recover, and little by little he resumed study.
translations.idiomatic: His students urged him to recover, and he gradually resumed instruction.

sentences.zh: 普通中，太尉臨川王宏臨州，召補祭酒從事，琛年已四十餘，始應辟命。

translations.literal: In the Putong period, the Grand Marshal Prince of Linchuan Hong governed the province and summoned him as Libationer Attendant; Chen was already over forty before he first accepted an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putong era, when the Grand Marshal Prince of Linchuan, Hong, took up his provincial post, he summoned Chen as Libationer Attendant. Chen was past forty before he accepted his first official summons.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞其有學術，召見文德殿，與語悅之，謂僕射徐勉曰：「琛殊有門業。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard that he had learning and summoned him to Wende Hall for an audience; pleased in conversation, he said to the Left Vice Director Xu Mian: "Chen truly has hereditary accomplishment."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of his scholarship, he summoned Chen to Wende Hall. Delighted by their conversation, he told Vice Director Xu Mian, "Chen is a worthy heir to a great scholarly house."

sentences.zh: 」仍補王國侍郎，稍遷兼中書通事舍人，參禮儀事。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed Attendant of the Princely State, and soon promoted to concurrent Palace Attendant of General Affairs in the Secretariat, participating in ritual matters.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed attendant of the princely establishment, then promoted to concurrent palace attendant for general affairs in the Secretariat, where he took part in deliberations on ritual.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞，詔琛撰新諡法，便即施用。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing; an edict ordered Chen to compile a new method of posthumous titles, which was put into use at once.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing. The emperor ordered him to draft a new system of posthumous titles, which went into immediate use.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子議大功之末，可以冠子嫁女。

translations.literal: At that time the Crown Prince debated that at the end of the period of greater mourning one might cap one's son and marry off one's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince argued that during the final days of greater mourning one might perform the capping ceremony for one's son and marry off one's daughter.

sentences.zh: 琛駁議曰：

translations.literal: Chen submitted a rebuttal, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chen submitted a counter-memorial, stating:

sentences.zh: 令旨以「大功之末，可得冠子嫁女，不得自冠自嫁」。

translations.literal: The order states that "at the end of greater mourning one may cap one's son and marry off one's daughter, but may not cap oneself or marry oneself off."
translations.idiomatic: Your directive holds that at the end of the greater mourning period one may cap one's son and marry off one's daughter, but may not perform one's own capping or one's own marriage.

sentences.zh: 推以記文，竊猶致惑。

translations.literal: Applying the Record text, I privately still find cause for doubt.
translations.idiomatic: When I weigh this against the Record, I remain privately puzzled.

sentences.zh: 案嫁冠之禮，本是父之所成。

translations.literal: Considering the rites of marriage and capping, they are originally what the father accomplishes.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage and capping rites are, in their nature, ceremonies that the father performs for the child.

sentences.zh: 無父之人，乃可自冠，故記稱大功小功，並以「冠子嫁子。

translations.literal: One without a father may cap himself; therefore the Record speaks of both greater and lesser mourning with the phrase "capping the son, marrying the son."
translations.idiomatic: Only someone without a father may cap himself. That is why the Record, in passages on both greater and lesser mourning, speaks of 'capping the son' and 'marrying the son.'

sentences.zh: 」為文，非關唯得為子，己身不得也。

translations.literal: " As wording, this does not concern only being allowed to act for the son while oneself is not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: " The wording does not mean that one may act only on the son's behalf while forbidding action on one's own account.

sentences.zh: 小功之末既得自嫁娶，而亦云：「冠子娶婦」，其義益明。

translations.literal: At the end of lesser mourning one may already marry and take a wife for oneself, yet it also says "capping the son, taking a wife for the son"—the meaning is all the clearer.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of lesser mourning one may already marry for oneself, yet the text also says 'cap the son, take a wife for the son'—which makes the principle even clearer.

sentences.zh: 故先列二服，每明冠子嫁子，結於後句，方顯自娶之義。

translations.literal: Therefore it first lists the two mourning grades, each clarifying capping the son and marrying the son; concluding in the later clause, it then displays the meaning of marrying for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The text first lists both mourning grades, each time specifying capping and marrying for the son, then closes with a final clause that reveals the right to marry for oneself.

sentences.zh: 既明小功自娶，即知大功自冠矣。

translations.literal: Since lesser mourning allows marrying for oneself, one knows that greater mourning allows capping for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Once lesser mourning is shown to permit marriage for oneself, it follows that greater mourning permits capping for oneself.

sentences.zh: 蓋是約言而見旨。

translations.literal: This is condensed wording that reveals the intent.
translations.idiomatic: This is abbreviated language that points to the underlying principle.

sentences.zh: 若謂緣父服大功，子服小功，小功服輕，故得為子冠嫁，大功服重，故不得自嫁自冠者，則小功之末，非明父子服殊，不應復云：「冠子嫁子。

translations.literal: If one holds that because the father wears greater mourning and the son wears lesser mourning, the lighter mourning allows capping and marrying for the son while the heavier mourning forbids marrying and capping for oneself, then at the end of lesser mourning—since it does not clarify that father and son wear different grades—it should not again say "capping the son, marrying the son."
translations.idiomatic: If the argument is that the father wears greater mourning while the son wears lesser mourning—that the lighter grade permits acting for the son while the heavier grade forbids acting for oneself—then at the end of lesser mourning the text, which does not distinguish father and son by grade, ought not repeat 'cap the son, marry the son.'

translations.literal: " [he should not say this].
translations.idiomatic: "—yet the Record does say exactly that.

sentences.zh: 若謂小功之文，言己可娶，大功之文，不言己冠，故知身有大功，不得自行嘉禮，但得為子冠嫁。

translations.literal: If one holds that the text on lesser mourning says one may marry for oneself, while the text on greater mourning does not say one may cap for oneself, and therefore knows that while wearing greater mourning one may not perform auspicious rites for oneself but may only cap and marry for the son—
translations.idiomatic: If the argument is that lesser mourning explicitly permits marriage for oneself while greater mourning does not mention capping for oneself, and therefore one wearing greater mourning may not perform auspicious rites for oneself but may only cap and marry for one's son—

sentences.zh: 竊謂有服不行嘉禮，本為吉凶不可相干。

translations.literal: I privately hold that wearing mourning and not performing auspicious rites is fundamentally because auspicious and inauspicious must not interfere with each other.
translations.idiomatic: I would say that the reason one in mourning does not perform auspicious rites is simply that auspicious and inauspicious occasions must not overlap.

sentences.zh: 子雖小功之末，可得行冠嫁，猶應須父得為其冠嫁。

translations.literal: Although at the end of lesser mourning the son may undergo capping and marriage, the father should still be the one who performs capping and marriage for him.
translations.idiomatic: Even if at the end of lesser mourning a son may receive capping and marriage, the father should still be the one who performs those rites for him.

sentences.zh: 若父于大功之末可以冠子嫁子，是於吉凶禮無礙；

translations.literal: If at the end of greater mourning the father may cap the son and marry the son, then auspicious and inauspicious rites do not interfere;
translations.idiomatic: If a father at the end of greater mourning may cap his son and marry off his daughter, then auspicious and inauspicious rites do not conflict;

sentences.zh: 吉凶禮無礙，豈不得自冠自嫁？

translations.literal: if auspicious and inauspicious rites do not interfere, how can one not be allowed to cap oneself and marry oneself off?
translations.idiomatic: and if they do not conflict, why should one not be permitted to cap oneself or marry for oneself?

sentences.zh: 若自冠自嫁於事有礙，則冠子嫁子寧獨可通？

translations.literal: If capping oneself and marrying oneself off is obstructed in the matter, how can capping the son and marrying the son alone be permissible?
translations.idiomatic: If capping or marrying for oneself is truly obstructed, how can capping or marrying for one's son alone be allowed?

sentences.zh: 今許其冠子而塞其自冠，是琛之所惑也。

translations.literal: Now to permit capping the son while blocking capping oneself—this is what Chen finds puzzling.
translations.idiomatic: To permit capping one's son while forbidding capping oneself—that is what puzzles me.

sentences.zh: 又令旨推「下殤小功不可娶婦，則降服大功亦不得為子冠嫁」。

translations.literal: Further, the order infers that "if at lesser mourning for a lower shang one may not take a wife, then at reduced greater mourning one also may not cap the son or marry the son."
translations.idiomatic: Your directive further infers that if the Record forbids marriage during lesser mourning for a lower shang death, then reduced greater mourning likewise forbids capping or marrying for one's son.

sentences.zh: 伏尋此旨，若為降服大功不可冠子嫁子，則降服小功亦不可自冠自嫁，是為凡厥降服大功小功皆不得冠娶矣。

translations.literal: Reverently examining this intent: if reduced greater mourning may not cap the son or marry the son, then reduced lesser mourning also may not cap or marry for oneself—in which case for all reduced greater and lesser mourning none may cap or marry.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considering this logic: if reduced greater mourning forbids capping or marrying for one's son, then reduced lesser mourning must also forbid capping or marrying for oneself—which would mean no capping or marrying is permitted under any reduced mourning grade.

sentences.zh: 記文應雲降服則不可，寧得唯稱下殤？

translations.literal: The Record text ought to say that reduced mourning is not permitted—how could it only name lower shang?
translations.idiomatic: The Record ought to say simply that reduced mourning forbids it—how could it name only lower shang?

sentences.zh: 今不言降服，的舉下殤，實有其義。

translations.literal: Now it does not speak of reduced mourning but precisely cites lower shang—there is in fact a reason.
translations.idiomatic: The text does not speak of reduced mourning in general but singles out lower shang—and there is good reason for that.

sentences.zh: 夫出嫁出後，或有再降，出後之身，于本姊妹降為大功，若是大夫服士父，又以尊降，則成小功，其於冠嫁義無以異。

translations.literal: When a daughter marries out or a son is adopted out, there may be a second reduction; the adopted-out person for natal sisters is reduced to greater mourning, and if a grandee wears mourning for a commoner's father there is further reduction by rank to lesser mourning—the principle for capping and marrying is no different.
translations.idiomatic: When a woman marries out or a son is given in adoption, mourning may be reduced a second time. An adopted son wears greater mourning for his natal sisters; if a grandee mourns a commoner father, rank reduces the obligation further to lesser mourning—yet the rules for capping and marrying remain the same.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，出嫁則有受我，出後則有傳重，並欲使薄於此而厚於彼。

translations.literal: The reason is that marrying out means another receives one, and adoption out means transmitting the weight of the line—both intend to make mourning lighter here and heavier there.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that marriage transfers a woman to another family and adoption transfers the weight of the ancestral line; in both cases mourning is lightened toward the natal family and deepened toward the new one.

sentences.zh: 此服雖降，彼服則隆。

translations.literal: This mourning is reduced, but that mourning is elevated.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning is reduced on one side even as it is heightened on the other.

sentences.zh: 昔實期親，雖復再降，猶依小功之禮，可冠可娶。

translations.literal: Formerly they were truly close kin; although mourning was reduced twice, they still followed lesser mourning rites and might cap and marry.
translations.idiomatic: They were once the closest kin; even after two reductions of mourning, the rules still follow lesser mourning, and capping and marriage remain permitted.

sentences.zh: 若夫期降大功，大功降為小功，止是一等，降殺有倫，服末嫁冠，故無有異。

translations.literal: If close mourning is reduced to greater mourning, and greater mourning reduced to lesser mourning, it is only one grade; the reduction has proper order, and at the end of mourning capping and marrying are the same—therefore there is no difference.
translations.idiomatic: When close mourning is reduced one grade to greater mourning, or greater mourning reduced one grade to lesser mourning, the reduction follows a clear hierarchy. At the end of mourning, capping and marriage are treated alike, and there is no difference.

sentences.zh: 唯下殤之服特明不娶之義者，蓋緣以幼弱之故。

translations.literal: Only for mourning of lower shang is the meaning of not marrying made specially clear—probably because of youth and weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Only for lower shang mourning does the text expressly forbid marriage—and that is because the deceased was young and frail.

sentences.zh: 夭喪情深，既無受厚他姓，又異傳重彼宗，嫌其年幼服輕，頓成殺略，故特明不娶，以示本重之恩。

translations.literal: Premature death stirs deep feeling; since there is no receiving into another surname's thickness, and it differs from transmitting weight to that lineage, fearing that youth makes the mourning light and would suddenly become curtailed reduction, therefore marriage is specially forbidden to show the original weight of affection.
translations.idiomatic: A child's untimely death awakens profound grief. There is no marriage into another clan to complicate the bond, nor adoption to shift the ancestral weight elsewhere. Lest the light mourning appropriate to a young child seem to diminish that grief too sharply, the text expressly forbids marriage to preserve the full depth of natal affection.

sentences.zh: 是以凡厥降服，冠嫁不殊，唯在下殤，乃明不娶。

translations.literal: Therefore for all reduced mourning, capping and marrying are not different; only for lower shang is not marrying made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Hence for every reduced mourning grade the rules for capping and marriage are the same; only lower shang expressly forbids marriage.

sentences.zh: 其義若此，則不得言大功之降服皆不冠嫁也。

translations.literal: If the meaning is thus, one cannot say that all reduced greater mourning may not cap or marry.
translations.idiomatic: On this reasoning, one cannot claim that every reduced grade of greater mourning forbids capping and marriage.

sentences.zh: 且記云：「下殤小功」，言下殤則不得通於中上，語小功又不兼于大功。

translations.literal: Moreover the Record says "lower shang, lesser mourning"; speaking of lower shang cannot extend to middle and upper, and speaking of lesser mourning does not include greater mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Record says 'lower shang, lesser mourning.' The mention of lower shang cannot extend to middle or upper shang, and the mention of lesser mourning cannot subsume greater mourning.

sentences.zh: 若實大功小功降服皆不冠嫁，上中二殤亦不冠嫁者，記不得直云：「下殤小功則不可」。

translations.literal: If in truth reduced greater and lesser mourning all may not cap or marry, and middle and upper shang also may not cap or marry, the Record could not simply say "lower shang, lesser mourning—then not permitted."
translations.idiomatic: If reduced greater and lesser mourning truly forbade all capping and marriage, and middle and upper shang did as well, the Record could not simply say 'lower shang, lesser mourning—not permitted.'

sentences.zh: 恐非文意，此又琛之所疑也。

translations.literal: I fear this is not the text's meaning—this too is what Chen doubts.
translations.idiomatic: That, I fear, would not be the text's meaning—and this too is what troubles me.

sentences.zh: 遂從琛議。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen's opinion was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Chen's position.

sentences.zh: 加員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 舊尚書南坐無貂，貂自琛始也。

translations.literal: Formerly at the southern seats of the Masters of Writing there was no sable tail; sable tails began with Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the southern benches of the Masters of Writing had no sable-tail insignia; Chen was the first to wear it.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，參禮儀如先。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Censor and participated in ritual matters as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to imperial censor and continued to take part in ritual deliberations as before.

sentences.zh: 琛性貪嗇，多受賕賂，家產既豐，買主第為宅，為有司奏，坐免官。

translations.literal: Chen was greedy and stingy by nature, often accepting bribes; once his family wealth was ample he bought the chief mansion as a residence, was memorialized by the relevant offices, and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was grasping by nature and took many bribes. When his household grew wealthy he purchased a chief minister's mansion for his home. The authorities memorialized against him, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 後為通直散騎常侍，領尚書左丞，參禮儀事。

translations.literal: Later he became Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Scattered Cavalry, continuing as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and participating in ritual matters.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as regular attendant for direct communication and scattered cavalry while retaining the post of left assistant director of the Masters of Writing and his role in ritual affairs.

sentences.zh: 琛前後居職，凡郊廟諸儀多所創定，每進見武帝，與語常移晷刻，故省中語曰：「上殿不下有賀雅。

translations.literal: In his successive offices Chen established many suburban and temple rites; each time he was received in audience by Emperor Wu their conversation often lasted past the hour-mark, so within the Secretariat they said: "Going up to the hall and not coming down—there is He the Elegant."
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his career Chen helped establish many suburban and temple rituals. Whenever he was received by Emperor Wu their conversation ran long past the hour, and within the Secretariat people joked, 'He goes up to the hall and never comes down—there's Elegant He.'

sentences.zh: 」琛容止閒雅，故時人呼之。

translations.literal: Chen's appearance and bearing were leisurely and refined; therefore people of the time called him thus.
translations.idiomatic: He Chen's graceful bearing and refined deportment earned him that nickname among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，參禮儀如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Cavalry Regular Chamberlain, participating in ritual matters as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was transferred to Attendant Cavalry Regular Chamberlain and continued to take part in ritual affairs as he had before.

sentences.zh: 時武帝年高，任職者緣飾奸諂，深害時政。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu was old in years; those holding office adorned themselves with treachery and flattery, deeply harming the governance of the age.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Wu had grown old, and officeholders cloaked themselves in sycophancy and deceit—a grave injury to public affairs.

sentences.zh: 琛啟陳事條封奏，大略：其一事曰，「今北邊稽服，政是生聚教訓之時，而天下戶口減落，誠當今之急務。

translations.literal: Chen submitted a memorial listing matters in separate sealed sections; the general outline: As for the first item, it said, 'Now the northern border submits and defers; this is precisely the time for gathering the people and teaching and instructing them, yet household registers under Heaven are decreasing and falling away—it is truly the urgent task of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: Chen submitted a sealed memorial outlining several points. The first ran roughly as follows: 'With the northern frontier now at peace, this should be a time to rebuild population and cultivate loyalty. Yet household registers across the empire keep shrinking—and that is the crisis of our day.

sentences.zh: 國家之于關外，賦稅蓋微，乃至年常租調，動致逋積，而人失安居，寧非牧守之過」。

translations.literal: As for the state in regard to territories beyond the passes, taxes and levies are largely light, yet even the annual regular rents and corvée assessments often lead to accumulated arrears, and the people lose peaceful dwelling—is this not the fault of governors and prefects?'
translations.idiomatic: 'Beyond the frontier passes the state's tax burden is light enough, yet annual rents and corvée levies still pile up unpaid. People lose their secure homes—is that not the fault of local governors and prefects?'

sentences.zh: 其二事曰，「今天下宰守所以皆尚貪殘，罕有廉白者，良由風俗侈靡使之然也。

translations.literal: The second item said, 'Today the chief ministers and prefects are all given to greed and cruelty; there are few who are clean and upright—this is truly because extravagant customs make them so.
translations.idiomatic: The second point argued that today's regional officials are almost universally greedy and cruel, with honest men the rare exception—and blamed decadent custom for making them so.

sentences.zh: 欲使人守廉隅，吏尚清白，安可得邪？

translations.literal: To wish to make people keep to clean corners and clerks esteem white integrity—how can this be obtained?'
translations.idiomatic: 'How can you expect officials to stay scrupulously honest when the culture rewards the opposite?'

sentences.zh: 今誠宜嚴為禁制，導之以節儉，貶黜雕飾，糾奏浮華，使眾皆知變其耳目，改其好惡，則易於反掌」。

translations.literal: Now it is truly fit that strict prohibitions be established, guiding them by frugality, demoting and dismissing carved ornamentation, impeaching and reporting flashy extravagance, so that the multitude all know to transform their ears and eyes and change their likes and dislikes—then it would be as easy as turning the palm.'
translations.idiomatic: 'What is needed now are tough bans on excess, leadership by example in frugality, penalties for ostentation, and exposure of hollow luxury—until everyone learns new tastes and new habits. Then reform would be as easy as flipping your hand.'

sentences.zh: 其三事曰，「鬥筲之人，詭競求進，運挈瓶之智，徼分外之求，以深刻為能，以繩逐為務，長弊增奸，實由於此。

translations.literal: The third item said, 'Petty-vessel men deviously compete seeking advancement, wielding the wisdom of carrying a bottle, seeking rewards outside their proper share, taking severity and harshness as competence, making relentless prosecution their task—longstanding harm and increasing villainy truly arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: The third indictment targeted petty schemers clawing for promotion—clever at small tricks, hungry for rewards out of proportion to their rank, proud of harshness and relentless at punishment. From such men, he argued, came deep corruption.

sentences.zh: 今誠願責其公平之效，黜其殘愚之心，則下安上謐，無徼幸之患矣」。

translations.literal: Now I truly wish that their effects of fairness be demanded, and their hearts of cruelty and folly be dismissed—then below would be settled and above would be tranquil, without the calamity of seeking undeserved luck.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Hold officials to fair outcomes, purge the instinct for cruelty and folly, and the lower ranks will be secure while the court stays calm—free of the disease of opportunism.'

sentences.zh: 其四事曰，「自征伐北境，帑藏空虛，今天下無事，而猶日不暇給者，良有以也。

translations.literal: The fourth item said, 'Since campaigns against the northern border, the treasury stores have been emptied; today there is no trouble under Heaven, yet still day after day there is no leisure to supply—there is truly a reason for this.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth warned that northern campaigns had drained the treasury. 'The realm is at peace now,' he wrote, 'yet the exchequer never catches up—there is a reason.'

sentences.zh: 夫國弊則省其事而息其費，事省則養人，費息則財聚。

translations.literal: When the state is exhausted then reduce its affairs and rest its expenditures; when affairs are reduced then nourish the people; when expenditures rest then wealth is gathered.
translations.idiomatic: 'When the state is strained, cut programs and stop waste. Cut programs and the people recover; stop waste and revenue accumulates.'

sentences.zh: 若言小費不足害財，則終年不息矣，以小役不足妨人，則終年不止矣」。

translations.literal: If one says small expenditures are insufficient to harm wealth, then the whole year would never rest; if small corvée is insufficient to obstruct people, then the whole year would never stop.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Say petty spending can't ruin the treasury, and spending never stops for a year. Say minor projects can't burden the people, and the people never get relief for a year.'

sentences.zh: 書奏，武帝大怒，召主書於前，口受敕責琛曰：「朕有天下四十餘年，公車讜言，日聞聽覽。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Wu was greatly angered. He summoned the chief clerk before him and orally received an edict rebuking Chen, saying: 'I have possessed All Under Heaven for more than forty years; memorials of forthright advice from the Public Chariot Office I hear day after day in my audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Emperor Wu exploded in rage. He called his chief clerk and dictated a rebuke to Chen: 'I've ruled for more than forty years and hear candid memorials every day from the petition office.

sentences.zh: 每苦倥傯，更增惛惑。

translations.literal: Each time I suffer from being overburdened and pressed; it only adds to my confusion and bewilderment.
translations.idiomatic: I'm already drowning in paperwork—it only leaves me more confused.

sentences.zh: 卿珥貂紆組，博問洽聞，不宜同於闒茸，止取名字，言我能上事，恨朝廷不能受。

translations.literal: You wear the sable fur and curved ribbons, broadly questioned and thoroughly informed—you should not be the same as coarse mediocrities, merely taking a name, saying 'I can submit upward memorials,' resenting that the court cannot accept them.
translations.idiomatic: You wear high rank and are supposed to be widely informed. Don't act like some provincial nonentity who only wants credit for 'speaking truth to power' and then whines that the court won't listen.

sentences.zh: 卿雲'今北邊稽服，政是生聚教訓之時，而人失安居，牧守之過'。

translations.literal: You said, 'Now the northern border submits and defers; this is precisely the time for gathering and nurturing—yet the people lose peaceful dwelling; it is the fault of governors and prefects.'
translations.idiomatic: You wrote that the north is pacified and this should be a time for nurturing the people, yet they have no peace—and that this is the fault of local governors.

sentences.zh: 但大澤之中有龍有蛇，縱不盡善，不能皆惡。

translations.literal: But in a great marsh there are both dragons and snakes; even if not all are good, they cannot all be evil.
translations.idiomatic: But in any large pool you'll find both dragons and snakes—not everyone is virtuous, but neither is everyone rotten.

sentences.zh: 卿可分明顯出其人。

translations.literal: You may clearly show forth these persons.
translations.idiomatic: Name them. Identify them clearly.

sentences.zh: 卿雲'宜導之以節儉'。

translations.literal: You said, 'They should be guided by frugality.'
translations.idiomatic: You advised guiding people toward thrift.

sentences.zh: 又云'至道者必以淳素為先'。

translations.literal: You also said, 'Those who reach the ultimate Way must take plain simplicity as foremost.'
translations.idiomatic: You also claimed that 'the man who attains the highest Way must put plain living first.'

sentences.zh: 此言大善。

translations.literal: These words are greatly good.
translations.idiomatic: Fine words—excellent doctrine.

sentences.zh: 夫子言'其身正，不令而行，其身不正，雖令不從'。

translations.literal: The Master said, 'When his person is upright, without giving orders things proceed; when his person is not upright, though orders are given, they are not followed.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: lead by example and people follow without commands; fail to lead and they won't obey no matter what you order.

sentences.zh: 朕絕房室三十餘年，不與女人同屋而寢亦三十餘年，于居處不過一床之地，雕飾之物不入于宮，此亦人所共知。

translations.literal: I have abstained from the inner chambers for more than thirty years, and for more than thirty years have not slept in the same room with women; in my dwelling I use no more than the space of one bed, carved ornamentation does not enter the palace—this too is known to all together.
translations.idiomatic: For over thirty years I have kept no harem and slept apart from women. My living quarters hold little more than a bed; no gaudy decoration enters my palace—and everyone knows it.

sentences.zh: 受生不飲酒，受生不好音聲，所以朝中曲宴未嘗奏樂。

translations.literal: From birth I do not drink wine; from birth I do not love sounds and music; therefore at palace banquets music has never been played.
translations.idiomatic: I've never touched wine and never cared for music—so palace feasts have never featured performances.

sentences.zh: 朕三更出理事，隨事多少。

translations.literal: I go out at the third watch to handle affairs, according to how many matters there are.
translations.idiomatic: I'm up before dawn handling business, as much as the day requires.

sentences.zh: 事或少，中前得竟，事多，至日昃方得就食。

translations.literal: If affairs are relatively few, before midday they can be finished; if affairs are many, only when the sun slants do I finish eating.
translations.idiomatic: On light days I'm done by noon; on heavy ones I eat only after the sun has begun to decline.

sentences.zh: 既常一食，若晝若夜，無有定時，疾苦之日，或亦再食。

translations.literal: Having constantly one meal, whether day or night without fixed time; on days of illness and pain, sometimes there are two meals.
translations.idiomatic: Usually I eat once, day or night, with no fixed hour; only when I'm ill do I sometimes take a second meal.

sentences.zh: 昔腰過於十圍，今之瘦削，裁二尺餘。

translations.literal: Formerly my waist exceeded ten girdle-circuits; now in my thinness and emaciation it is barely more than two feet and change.
translations.idiomatic: Once my waist measured more than ten girths around; now I'm so wasted it is barely two feet and a bit.

sentences.zh: 舊帶猶存，非為妄說。

translations.literal: The old belt still exists—it is not a vain saying.
translations.idiomatic: The old belt still hangs there—I'm not making this up.

sentences.zh: 為誰為之？

translations.literal: For whom was it done? For whom?
translations.idiomatic: Who did I do this for?

sentences.zh: 救物故也。

translations.literal: To rescue things, that is why.
translations.idiomatic: To rescue the realm—that is why.

sentences.zh: 書雲，'股肱惟人，良臣惟聖'。

translations.literal: The Documents says, 'The arms and legs are the people; good ministers are what makes a sage.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: 'The people's arms and legs are ministers; sage rule depends on good ministers.'

sentences.zh: 向使朕有股肱，可得中主，今乃不免居九品之下。

translations.literal: If formerly I had arms and legs, I could have reached being a middling lord; now I cannot avoid ranking below the ninth grade.
translations.idiomatic: With true ministers I might have been a passable ruler; as it is I'm no better than the lowest sort of sovereign.

sentences.zh: '不令而行'，徒虛言耳。

translations.literal: 'Without giving orders things proceed'—empty words only.
translations.idiomatic: 'Lead by example and people follow'—mere talk, in my case.

sentences.zh: 卿又云'百司莫不奏事，詭競求進'。

translations.literal: You also said, 'All the hundred offices none fail to submit memorials, deviously competing seeking advancement.'
translations.idiomatic: You also complained that every office floods me with memorials as officials claw for promotion.

sentences.zh: 今不許外人呈事，於義可否？

translations.literal: Now if outside persons are not allowed to submit memorials—is this right in principle or not?
translations.idiomatic: So tell me: should outsiders be barred from memorializing—is that proper?

sentences.zh: 以噎廢餐，此之謂也。

translations.literal: To abandon eating because of choking—this is what it is called.
translations.idiomatic: That's like refusing to eat ever again because you once choked.

sentences.zh: 若斷呈事，誰屍其任？

translations.literal: If submitting memorials is cut off—who will take charge of the responsibility?
translations.idiomatic: Stop all memorials and who carries the work?

sentences.zh: 專委之人，云何可得？

translations.literal: The persons specially entrusted—how can they be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: And where will you find officials you can wholly trust?

sentences.zh: 是故古人云，'專聽生奸，獨任成亂'。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients said, 'Exclusive listening breeds treachery; sole reliance completes disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: That's why the ancients warned: 'Hearing only one voice breeds intrigue; relying on one man invites chaos.'

sentences.zh: 何者是宜，具以奏聞。

translations.literal: Which things are suitable—fully set them forth in memorial and inform Us.
translations.idiomatic: Tell me exactly what you think should be done—memorialize the specifics.

sentences.zh: 」琛奉敕但謝過而已，不敢有所指斥。

translations.literal: Chen received the edict and only apologized for fault, not daring to have any pointing out or denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: Chen took the rebuke and apologized, daring not name a single culprit.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，為中軍宣城王長史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping, he served as Chief Assistant to the Central Army of Prince Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping, he became chief secretary to the Central Army under Prince Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 侯景陷城，琛被創未死，賊求得之，輿至闕下，求見僕射王克、領軍朱異，勸開城納賊。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing captured the city, Chen received wounds but did not die; the rebels sought and obtained him, carried him in a litter to below the palace gate, sought audience with Vice Director Wang Ke and Commander of the Palace Guard Zhu Yi, urging opening the city to admit the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing broke into the city Chen was wounded but survived. The rebels found him, carried him to the palace gate, and insisted on seeing Vice Director Wang Ke and Guard Commander Zhu Yi to press them to surrender the city.

sentences.zh: 克等讓之，涕泣而止。

translations.literal: Ke and the others reproached him; weeping, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke and the others upbraided him until he broke down in tears and desisted.

sentences.zh: 賊復輿送莊嚴寺療之。

translations.literal: The rebels again carried him in a litter and sent him to Zhuangyan Temple to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then had him taken to Zhuangyan Temple for treatment.

sentences.zh: 明年，台城不守，琛逃歸鄉里。

translations.literal: The next year, the capital did not hold; Chen fled back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the capital fell, Chen escaped to his native place.

sentences.zh: 其年，賊寇會稽，復執琛送出都，以為金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That same year, when the rebels raided Kuaiji, they again seized Chen and sent him out to the capital, appointing him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Later that year, when the rebels overran Kuaiji, they captured Chen again, sent him back to the capital, and made him Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 琛所撰三禮講疏、五經滯義及諸儀注凡百餘篇。

translations.literal: What Chen authored included commentaries on the Three Ritual Classics, discussions resolving difficulties in the Five Classics, and various ritual regulations—in all more than a hundred chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's writings included commentaries on the Three Rituals, essays resolving cruxes in the Five Classics, and numerous ritual manuals—more than a hundred works in all.

sentences.zh: 子翊，位巴山太守。

translations.literal: His son Yi held the position of Administrator of Bashan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi became prefect of Bashan.

sentences.zh: 司馬褧字元表，河內溫人也。

translations.literal: Sima Jiong, styled Yuanbiao, was a man of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong, whose courtesy name was Yuanbiao, came from Wen county in Henei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖純之，晉大司農高密敬王。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chunzhi was Grand Minister of Finance and Prince Gong of Gaomi in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chunzhi served Jin as Grand Minister of Finance and held the posthumous title Prince Gong of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 祖讓之，員外常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rangzhi was External Member Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rangzhi was an external member of the Attendant Cavalier office.

sentences.zh: 父燮，善三禮，仕齊位國子博士。

translations.literal: His father Xie was skilled in the Three Rituals and served Qi as Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie mastered the Three Rituals and served the Qi as a National University erudite.

sentences.zh: 褧少傳家業，強力專精，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Jiong in youth transmitted the family profession, with strong effort concentrated and refined, his hand not releasing the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Jiong inherited the family scholarship, studying with tireless focus and seldom setting a book down.

sentences.zh: 沛國劉瓛為儒者宗，嘉其學，深相賞好。

translations.literal: Liu Huan of Pei was patriarch of the Ru scholars; he admired his learning and deeply reciprocated appreciation and fondness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan of Pei commanded the respect of Confucian scholars; he admired Jiong's learning and became a close friend.

sentences.zh: 與樂安任昉善，昉亦推重之。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Ren Fang of Le'an; Fang also pushed and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also close to Ren Fang of Le'an, who held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，詔通儒定五禮，有舉褧修嘉禮，除尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian in Liang, an edict ordered broadly learned men to fix the Five Rituals; there was a recommendation of Jiong to compile the Auspicious Rituals, and he was appointed Lang of the Sacrificial Worship Section of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang Tianjian era, the court ordered eminent scholars to codify the Five Rituals. Jiong was recommended to compile the Auspicious Rites section and was made a secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時創定禮樂，褧所建議，多見施行。

translations.literal: At that time the rites and music were newly fixed; Jiong's proposed recommendations many were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: As new ritual and music codes were drafted, many of Jiong's proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 兼中書通事舍人，每吉凶禮，當時名儒明山賓、賀瑒等疑不能斷者，皆取決焉。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Palace Secretariat Attendant-in-General; whenever for auspicious or inauspicious rites the famed Ru scholars Ming Shanbin, He Yang, and others had doubts they could not resolve, all took Jiong's decision.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as a palace secretariat attendant. Whenever eminent scholars such as Ming Shanbin and He Yang could not settle a ritual question, they deferred to Jiong.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become chief censor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，出為宣毅南康王長史，行府國並石頭戍軍事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he went out as Chief Assistant to Prince Xuan of Nankang, concurrently administering the princely fief and the military affairs of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he left the capital to serve as chief secretary to Prince Xuan of Nankang, overseeing the princely domain and the Shitou fortress garrison.

sentences.zh: 褧雖居外官，有敕預文德、武德二殿長名問訊，不限日。

translations.literal: Although Jiong held an outside office, there was an edict ordering him to participate in the long-name salutations at the Wende and Wude Halls, without limit on days.
translations.idiomatic: Though posted outside the capital, he received orders to attend the regular audience rolls at Wende and Wude halls whenever summoned.

sentences.zh: 遷晉安王長史，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Assistant to the Prince of Jin'an, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to chief secretary under the Prince of Jin'an and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 王命記室庾肩吾集其文為十卷。

translations.literal: The prince ordered Recorder Yu Jianwu to collect his writings into ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had his recorder Yu Jianwu compile his writings into ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 所撰嘉禮儀注一百一十六卷。

translations.literal: What he authored, the Auspicious Rites regulations and commentaries, totaled one hundred sixteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His Auspicious Rites manual alone ran to one hundred sixteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 朱異字彥和，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Yi, styled Yanhe, was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yi, courtesy name Yanhe, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖昭之，以學解稱於鄉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhaozhi was famed in the district for scholarly understanding.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhaozhi was known locally as a scholar of wide learning.

sentences.zh: 叔父謙之字處光，以義烈知名。

translations.literal: His uncle Qianzhi, styled Chuguang, was famed for righteous valor.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Qianzhi, styled Chuguang, won fame for courage in a just cause.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，所生母亡，昭之假葬于田側，為族人朱幼方燎火所焚。

translations.literal: When he was several years old, his birth mother died; Zhaozhi provisionally buried her at the side of a field, and she was burned by fire set by clansman Zhu Youfang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianzhi was still a small boy his mother died. Zhaozhi buried her temporarily in a field, and a kinsman, Zhu Youfang, burned the grave with a brush fire.

sentences.zh: 同產姊密語之，謙之雖小，便哀感如持喪，長不昏娶。

translations.literal: His full sister spoke to him in private; though Qianzhi was small, at once he grieved as if in mourning, and when grown never married.
translations.idiomatic: His sister told him the truth in secret. Though still a child, Qianzhi mourned as if for a full funeral and never married as an adult.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，手刃殺幼方，詣獄自系。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era of Qi, with his own hand he blade-killed Youfang and went to prison to bind himself.
translations.idiomatic: During Qi's Yongming era he killed Youfang himself and turned himself in.

sentences.zh: 縣令申靈勖表上之。

translations.literal: The district magistrate Shen Lingxu memorialized upward regarding it.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate Shen Lingxu reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝嘉其義，慮相報復，乃遣謙之隨曹武西行。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi admired his righteousness, fearing mutual retaliation, then sent Qianzhi to follow Cao Wu westward.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi praised his loyalty but, fearing a blood feud, ordered Qianzhi to leave with Cao Wu on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 將發，幼方子懌于津陽門伺殺謙之。

translations.literal: About to set out, Youfang's son Yi waited at Jinyang Gate and assassinated Qianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Just before departure Youfang's son Yi ambushed Qianzhi at Jinyang Gate and killed him.

sentences.zh: 謙之兄巽之，即異父也，又刺殺懌。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's elder brother Xunzhi, who was Yi's father on a different side, again stabbed and killed Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's older brother Xunzhi—Yi's uncle by marriage—then killed Yi in turn.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞。

translations.literal: The responsible offices reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported the case to the court.

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「此皆是義事，不可問。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said: 'These all are righteous matters—not to be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said: 'These are all acts of righteousness—there will be no prosecution.

sentences.zh: 」悉赦之。

translations.literal: All were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 吳興沈顗聞而歎曰：「弟死于孝，兄殉于義，孝友之節，萃此一門。

translations.literal: Shen Yan of Wuxing heard and sighed, saying: 'The younger brother died in filial piety, the elder brother died for righteousness—filial and fraternal integrity gathered in this one gate.'
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Yan of Wuxing heard the news he sighed: 'One brother died for filial duty, the other for righteousness—both virtues in a single family.'

sentences.zh: 」巽之字處林，有志節，著辯相論。

translations.literal: Xunzhi, styled Chulin, had will and integrity, and authored Discourse on Physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi, styled Chulin, was a man of principle and wrote the Discourse on Physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 幼時，顧歡見而異之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: When young, Gu Huan saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he impressed Gu Huan, who gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 仕齊官至吳平令。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he reached the office of Magistrate of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he rose to magistrate of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 異年數歲，外祖顧歡撫之，謂其祖昭之曰：「此兒非常器，當成卿門戶。

translations.literal: When Yi was several years old, his maternal grandfather Gu Huan dandled him and said to his grandfather Zhaozhi: 'This boy is no ordinary vessel—he will succeed to your gate and household.'
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yi was still small his maternal grandfather Gu Huan fondled him and told Zhaozhi: 'This child is no ordinary talent—he will bring honor to your clan.'

sentences.zh: 」年十餘，好群聚蒱博，頗為鄉黨所患。

translations.literal: In his teens he loved gathering in groups for dice games, and was rather a pest to the village community.
translations.idiomatic: As a teenager he ran with gambling circles and was something of a nuisance in the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 及長，乃折節從師。

translations.literal: When he reached adulthood, then he corrected his conduct and followed teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown, he reformed himself and turned to serious study.

sentences.zh: 梁初開五館，異服膺于博士明山賓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, the Five Academies were opened; Yi devoted himself to the Erudite Ming Shanbin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang opened its Five Academies, Yi became a devoted student of the erudite Ming Shanbin.

sentences.zh: 居貧，以傭書自業，寫畢便誦。

translations.literal: Living in poverty, he took copying books as his profession; when finished writing he at once recited.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he supported himself by copying books and would recite each text from memory as soon as he finished.

sentences.zh: 遍覽五經，尤明禮、易。

translations.literal: He read through the Five Classics, especially clear in Rituals and Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Five Classics and was especially strong in Rituals and the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 涉獵文史，兼通雜藝，博弈書算，皆其所長。

translations.literal: He ranged through literary and historical writings, and concurrently penetrated miscellaneous arts—weiqi, games, calligraphy, and calculation were all his strong points.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in literature and history and had a gift for practical arts as well—board games, calligraphy, and arithmetic among them.

sentences.zh: 年二十，出都詣尚書令沈約，面試之，因戲異曰：「卿年少，何乃不廉？

translations.literal: At twenty, he went out to the capital and called on Minister of the Interior Shen Yue; Yue tested him face to face, and in jest said to Yi: 'You are young—why are you not clean?'
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he traveled to the capital to meet Minister Shen Yue, who examined him and teased: 'You're so young—how can you be so greedy?'

sentences.zh: 」異逡巡未達其旨，約乃曰：「天下唯有文義棋書，卿一時將去，可謂不廉也。

translations.literal: Yi hesitated and did not reach his intent; Yue then said: 'Under Heaven there are only literary arts, principles, weiqi, and books—for a moment you took them all away; one could call this not being clean.'
translations.idiomatic: Yi didn't catch the joke at first, so Shen Yue explained: 'Literature, philosophy, chess, calligraphy—the whole world has only those pursuits, and you've scooped them all up at once. I'd call that greedy.'

sentences.zh: 」尋上書言建康宜置獄司，比廷尉。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial saying Jiankang should establish a prison office, comparable to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized that the capital should establish a prison office on a par with the central Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 敕付尚書詳議，從之。

translations.literal: An edict was entrusted to the Ministry of the Interior for detailed deliberation; it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne referred the plan to the ministry for review and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 舊制，年二十五方得釋褐，時異適二十一，特敕擢為揚州議曹從事史。

translations.literal: By old regulation, one had to be twenty-five to remove rough clothes and take office; at that time Yi was just twenty-one, but by special edict he was elevated to Attendant Clerk of the Yangzhou Consultative Council.
translations.idiomatic: The usual rule barred men from entering office before twenty-five; Yi was only twenty-one when a special decree made him a staff officer on the Yangzhou advisory council.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔求異能之士，五經博士明山賓表薦異：「年時尚少，德備老成，在獨無散逸之想，處闇有對賓之色。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict seeking men of unusual ability; the Five Classics Erudite Ming Shanbin memorialized recommending Yi: 'His years are still young, but his virtue is complete like an old man; alone he has no thought of dissipation, in darkness he has the bearing of one facing guests.'
translations.idiomatic: When the court called for men of exceptional talent, Ming Shanbin recommended him: 'Still young in years, he has the steadiness of maturity. In solitude he keeps his discipline; even in private he carries himself as if before company.'

sentences.zh: 器宇弘深，神表峰峻。

translations.literal: His vessel and bearing are vast and deep; his spirit and appearance peak and lofty.
translations.idiomatic: His capacity is broad and his bearing imposing; his spirit rises like a summit.

sentences.zh: 金山萬丈，緣陟未登；

translations.literal: A gold mountain ten thousand zhang high—climbing by its paths, he has yet to ascend;
translations.idiomatic: Like a ten-thousand-zhang golden mountain whose paths he has not yet climbed to the top—

sentences.zh: 玉海千尋，窺映不測。

translations.literal: A jade sea a thousand xun deep—glimpsing its reflections, one cannot fathom them.
translations.idiomatic: His depth is like a jade ocean a thousand fathoms deep—one catches glimpses but cannot plumb it.

sentences.zh: 加以珪璋新琢，錦組初構，觸響鏗鏘，遇采便發。

translations.literal: Moreover, a newly carved jade tablet and silk brocade newly woven—when touched they ring clearly; encountering opportunity their brilliance at once emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Freshly polished like sacred jade, newly woven like brocade, he rings true at a touch and shines the moment opportunity appears.

sentences.zh: 觀其信行，非唯十室所稀，若使負重遙途，必有千里之用。

translations.literal: Observing his integrity and conduct, he is not merely rare in ten households; if made to bear heavy burdens on a long road, he would surely have use for a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: His trustworthiness and conduct are rare even among many neighbors; given heavy responsibility over a long haul, he would prove useful a thousand miles away.

sentences.zh: 」武帝召見，使說孝經、周易義，甚悅之，謂左右曰：「朱異實異。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu summoned him for an audience, had him expound the meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety and the Book of Changes, and was greatly pleased; he said to those around him: 'Zhu Yi is truly unusual.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu received him in audience and had him lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Book of Changes. He was delighted and told his attendants, 'Zhu Yi truly lives up to that name—he is exceptional.'

sentences.zh: 」後見明山賓曰：「卿所舉殊得人。

translations.literal: Later he saw Ming Shanbin and said: 'The man you recommended is an especially apt choice.'
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor told Ming Shanbin, 'You recommended exactly the right man.'

sentences.zh: 」仍召直西省，俄兼太學博士。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was summoned to serve directly in the Western Bureau; soon he concurrently held the position of Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was then assigned to the Western Secretariat and soon added the post of academy erudite.

sentences.zh: 其年，帝自講孝經，使異執讀。

translations.literal: That year, the Emperor personally lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and had Yi hold the text and read.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, when the emperor lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety himself, Yi was appointed to read the text aloud.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書儀曹郎，入兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Lang of the Protocol Section of the Ministry of the Interior, and entered to concurrently serve as Communicating Affairs Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to a post in the ministry's ceremonial office and also served as a secretariat attendant handling imperial communications.

sentences.zh: 後除中書郎，時秋日，始拜，有飛蟬正集異武冠上，時咸謂蟬珥之兆。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Lang of the Secretariat; it was autumn, and when he first took office a flying cicada just alighted on Yi's military cap—all at the time said it was an omen of the cicada ear pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later, upon his appointment as a secretariat director in autumn, a cicada landed on his official cap as he took office—everyone took it as a sign of high promotion.

sentences.zh: 遷太子右衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commandant of the crown prince's right guard.

sentences.zh: 普通五年，大舉北侵，魏徐州刺史元法僧遣使請舉地內屬，詔有司議其虛實。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Putong, a major northern campaign was launched; Wei Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng sent envoys requesting to surrender his territory and submit to the dynasty; an edict ordered the relevant offices to deliberate on whether it was genuine or false.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year 5, as Liang launched a major northern offensive, Yuan Faseng, the Wei governor of Xuzhou, sent envoys offering to defect with his territory. The throne ordered officials to assess whether the offer was genuine.

sentences.zh: 異曰：「自王師北討，克獲相繼，徐州地轉削弱，咸願歸罪。

translations.literal: Yi said: 'Since the royal army marched north to punish, captures and victories have followed one after another; Xuzhou's territory has steadily weakened, and all wish to bring guilt upon themselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Yi argued: 'Since our armies marched north, victory has followed victory and Xuzhou has grown weaker. Its people all wish to surrender and accept punishment.'

sentences.zh: 法僧懼禍，其降必非偽也。

translations.literal: Faseng fears disaster; his surrender surely is not feigned.'
translations.idiomatic: Faseng is afraid of disaster—his surrender cannot be a ruse.'

sentences.zh: 」帝仍遣異報法僧，並敕眾軍應接，受異節度。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon dispatched Yi to reply to Faseng, and concurrently ordered the various armies to support and receive him, placing them under Yi's command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yi to respond to Faseng and ordered all armies supporting the operation to follow Yi's command.

sentences.zh: 及至，法僧遵承朝旨，如異策焉。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Faseng obeyed and accepted the court's directive, just as Yi had planned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi arrived, Faseng complied with the court's orders exactly as Yi had predicted.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant Cavalryman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regular attendant-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 異容貌魁梧，能舉止，雖出自諸生，甚閑軍國故實。

translations.literal: Yi's appearance was towering and imposing, his bearing capable; though coming from among the scholars, he was very familiar with old precedents of military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing in bearing, Yi carried himself well. Though trained as a scholar, he knew military and administrative precedent inside out.

sentences.zh: 自周舍卒後，異代掌機密，其軍旅謀謨，方鎮改換，朝儀國典，詔誥敕書，並典掌之。

translations.literal: From after Zhou She's death, Yi in his stead managed secret affairs: military campaigns and strategies, changes of regional commanders, court ritual and state statutes, edicts, announcements, and imperial letters—all were under his charge.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou She died, Yi took charge of confidential state business—military planning, provincial appointments, court ritual, state law, and all edicts and imperial correspondence.

sentences.zh: 每四方表疏，當局簿領，諮詳請斷，填委於前，異屬辭落紙，覽事下議，縱橫敏贍，不暫停筆，頃刻之間，諸事便了。

translations.literal: Whenever memorials arrived from the four directions, or the bureaus' ledgers and requests for consultation and decision piled up before him, Yi would compose words onto paper, review affairs and send them down for discussion—moving freely, sharp and ample, not pausing his brush for an instant; in the space of a moment, all matters were finished.
translations.idiomatic: When memorials from every province and stacks of bureau paperwork requiring decisions piled up before him, Yi wrote without pause—drafting, reviewing, and dispatching items for deliberation with swift, fluent ease. In moments, the whole backlog was cleared.

sentences.zh: 遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 啟求於儀賢堂奉述武帝老子義，敕許之。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to expound Emperor Wu's interpretation of the Laozi at the Hall of Esteemed Worthies; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to lecture on the emperor's interpretation of the Laozi in the Hall of Esteemed Worthies, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 及就講，朝士及道俗聽者千餘人，為一時之盛。

translations.literal: When the lecture was delivered, more than a thousand court officials and both clergy and laity came to listen—it was the grand occasion of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When he delivered the lectures, more than a thousand court officials, clergy, and lay listeners attended—a spectacle of the age.

sentences.zh: 時城西又開士林館以延學士，異與左丞賀琛遞日述武帝禮記中庸義。

translations.literal: At that time the Scholarly Grove Hall west of the city was also opened to host scholars; Yi and Left Assistant He Chen lectured on alternate days on Emperor Wu's interpretation of the Doctrine of the Mean in the Record of Rituals.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time the Scholarly Grove Hall opened west of the city to host learned men; Yi and the left vice minister He Chen alternated days lecturing on the emperor's exposition of the Doctrine of the Mean.

sentences.zh: 皇太子又召異于玄圃講易。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince also summoned Yi to the Dark Garden to lecture on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince also invited Yi to lecture on the Book of Changes in the Dark Garden.

sentences.zh: 大同八年，改加侍中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, he was promoted and additionally given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 8 he was made a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 異博解多藝，圍碁上品，而貪財冒賄，欺罔視聽，以伺候人主意，不肯進賢黜惡。

translations.literal: Yi was broadly learned and skilled in many arts, top rank at weiqi; yet he was greedy for wealth and accepted bribes, deceived and misled what the eyes and ears of the ruler perceived, in order to watch and await the sovereign's intentions, and would not advance the worthy or dismiss the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was widely learned and a master of many arts, including top-rank weiqi—but he was greedy, took bribes, and shaped what reached the emperor's eyes and ears to suit the ruler's mood, never promoting talent or removing the corrupt.

sentences.zh: 四方餉饋，曾無推拒，故遠近莫不忿疾。

translations.literal: Gifts sent from the four directions—he never once pushed them away; hence near and far, none did not resent and loathe him.
translations.idiomatic: He never refused gifts from anyone anywhere, so resentment spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 起宅東陂，窮乎美麗，晚日來下，酣飲其中。

translations.literal: He built a residence at East Dam, exhaustively beautiful; when the late sun descended, he drank deeply within it.
translations.idiomatic: He built a lavish estate at East Dam and spent his evenings there drinking deep as the sun went down.

sentences.zh: 每迫曛黃，慮台門將闔，乃引其鹵簿自宅至城，使捉城門停留管鑰。

translations.literal: Whenever dusk drew near, fearing the palace gate would close, he would lead his guard of honor from his residence to the city and have them seize the city gate, hold it open, and keep the keys.
translations.idiomatic: As dusk approached and he feared the palace gates would close, he marched his full guard procession from home to the city wall and had them hold the gate open and keep the keys.

sentences.zh: 既而聲勢所驅，熏灼內外，產與羊侃相埒。

translations.literal: Before long, driven by the force of his prestige, he scorched inside and outside; his estate was the equal of Yang Kan's.
translations.idiomatic: His power soon burned hot inside the court and out, and his wealth matched that of Yang Kan.

sentences.zh: 好飲食，極滋味聲色之娛，子鵝炰鰌不輟於口，雖朝謁，從車中必齎飴餌。

translations.literal: He loved food and drink, exhausting the pleasures of flavors, sounds, and colors; young goose and stewed loach never ceased from his mouth; even when attending court audience, from his carriage he always carried sweetmeats.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged every pleasure of food, wine, music, and women—young goose and braised loach constantly on his lips—and even brought sweets in his carriage to court audiences.

sentences.zh: 而輕傲朝賢，不避貴戚。

translations.literal: Yet he treated court worthies lightly and disdainfully, not avoiding even the imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he treated court elites with open disdain, showing no deference even to the highest nobles.

sentences.zh: 人或誨之，異曰：「我寒士也，遭逢以至今日。
