translations.literal: When someone admonished him, Yi said: 'I am a humble scholar who reached today through fortunate encounter.'
translations.idiomatic: When someone cautioned him, Yi replied, 'I came from humble ranks and rose by luck alone.'

sentences.zh: 諸貴皆恃枯骨見輕，我下之，則為蔑尤甚。

translations.literal: All the nobles rely on dried bones and see others lightly; if I defer to them, the contempt would be even greater.'
translations.idiomatic: The great families look down on everyone because of their dead ancestors' bones. If I bow to them, they'd despise me all the more.'

sentences.zh: 我是以先之。」

translations.literal: That is why I go ahead of them.'
translations.idiomatic: So I snub them first.'

sentences.zh: 自徐勉、周舍卒後，外朝則何敬容，內省則異。

translations.literal: From after Xu Mian's and Zhou She's deaths, for the outer court there was He Jingrong; for the inner secretariat, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Mian and Zhou She died, He Jingrong ran the outer court and Yi the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敬容質愨無文，以綱維為己任，異文華敏洽，曲營世譽，二人行異而俱見幸。

translations.literal: Jingrong was plain and sincere without ornament, taking maintaining the framework as his own task; Yi was literary, florid, sharp, and affable, curving to cultivate worldly reputation—the two men's conduct differed, yet both were favored.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong was plain and dutiful, devoted to keeping the machinery of government running; Yi was brilliant, quick-witted, and bent on worldly acclaim. Their styles differed, but both enjoyed imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 異在內省十餘年，未嘗被譴。

translations.literal: Yi was in the inner secretariat for more than ten years and never once was reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served in the inner secretariat more than ten years without a single rebuke.

sentences.zh: 司農卿傅岐嘗謂異曰：「今聖上委政于君，安得每事從旨。

translations.literal: Minister of Finance Fu Qi once said to Yi: 'Now the sage sovereign has entrusted governance to you—how can you on every matter follow his wishes?'
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qi, minister of finance, once told Yi: 'The emperor has entrusted you with real authority—how can you simply agree with everything he wants?'

sentences.zh: 頃者外聞殊有異論。

translations.literal: Recently outside there have been quite unusual opinions.'
translations.idiomatic: People outside the palace are already talking.'

sentences.zh: 」異曰：「政言我不能諫爭耳。

translations.literal: Yi said: 'They are simply saying I cannot remonstrate and dispute.'
translations.idiomatic: Yi answered: 'They're saying I don't remonstrate with him.'

sentences.zh: 當今天子聖明，吾豈可以其所聞幹忤天聽。」

translations.literal: The present Son of Heaven is sage and enlightened—how could I take what they have heard and offend against Heaven's audience?'
translations.idiomatic: Our ruler is wise and enlightened. How could I trouble his ears with gossip from outsiders?'

sentences.zh: 太清二年，為中領軍，舍人如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, he became Central Commander of the Army; his gentleman's post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing year 2 he became central army commander while retaining his attendant post.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝夢中原盡平，舉朝稱慶，甚悅，以語異曰：「吾生平少夢，夢必有實。

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Wu dreamed that the Central Plains were entirely pacified; the whole court proclaimed congratulations, and he was very pleased; he told Yi: 'In my life I seldom dream—when I dream, it surely comes true.'
translations.idiomatic: Early on the emperor dreamed that the Central Plains had been wholly pacified. The whole court congratulated him, and he was delighted. He told Yi, 'I rarely dream in my life—and when I do, it comes true.'

sentences.zh: 」異曰：「此宇內方一之征。

translations.literal: Yi said: 'This is a sign that within the four seas unity is being squared.'
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, 'This is a sign the realm is about to be unified.'

sentences.zh: 」及侯景降，敕召群臣廷議，尚書僕射謝舉等以為不可許。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered, an edict summoned the ministers for court deliberation; Vice Minister of the Interior Xie Ju and others held that he should not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing offered to defect, the emperor convened the court for debate. Vice Minister Xie Ju and others argued that he should not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 武帝欲納之，未決，嘗夙興至武德合口，獨言：「我國家猶若金甌，無一傷缺，承平若此，今便受地，詎是事宜？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu wished to accept him but had not decided; once at dawn he went to the mouth of Wude Gate and spoke alone: 'Our state is still like a golden bowl, without a single wound or break; peace is like this—now to accept territory at once, how could it be a suitable affair?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to accept but could not decide. One morning at dawn he went alone to Wude Gate and murmured: 'Our realm is still whole, like a golden bowl without a crack, and peace reigns as it does—should we really take his land now?'

sentences.zh: 脫至紛紜，悔無所及。

translations.literal: If it comes to disorder, regret will reach nowhere.'
translations.idiomatic: If trouble follows, it will be too late for regret.'

sentences.zh: 」異探帝微旨，答曰：「聖明禦宇，上應蒼玄，北土遺黎，誰不慕仰，為無機會，未達其心。

translations.literal: Yi, sensing the Emperor's hidden intent, answered: 'Sagely and enlightened, he rules the realm, above responding to the azure darkness; the remnant people of the north—who does not admire and look up? Only for lack of opportunity have they not reached their heart's wish.'
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's mind, Yi answered: 'Your sage rule answers Heaven. Every survivor in the north looks to you with longing—they simply lacked the chance.'

sentences.zh: 今侯景分魏國太半，遠歸聖朝；

translations.literal: Now Hou Jing has divided more than half of Wei and come from afar to return to the holy court;
translations.idiomatic: Now Hou Jing brings more than half of Wei and returns to our court from afar;

sentences.zh: 若不容受，恐絕後來之望。

translations.literal: If we do not accept and accommodate him, I fear we will cut off the hopes of those who come after.'
translations.idiomatic: If we refuse him, we may kill the hopes of others who would follow.'

sentences.zh: 」帝深納異言，又感前夢，遂納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply accepted Yi's words, and also moved by the earlier dream, thereupon accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Yi's advice to heart, remembered his dream, and accepted Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 及貞陽侯敗沒，帝憂曰：「今勿作晉家事乎？

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Zhenyang was defeated and captured, the Emperor worried and said: 'Are we not now repeating the affairs of Jin?'
translations.idiomatic: When the Marquis of Zhenyang was defeated and captured, the emperor worried aloud: 'Are we reliving what happened to the Jin dynasty?'

sentences.zh: 」尋而貞陽自魏遣使述魏相高澄欲申和睦。

translations.literal: Soon Zhenyang, from Wei, sent envoys describing that Wei Chancellor Gao Cheng wished to renew harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhenyang sent envoys from Wei saying Chancellor Gao Cheng wanted to restore good relations.

sentences.zh: 敕有司定議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to decide by deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 異又議以和為允，帝從之。

translations.literal: Yi again deliberated that peace was acceptable; the Emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi again argued for peace, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，遣建康令謝挺、通直郎徐陵使北通好。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month, he dispatched Jiankang Magistrate Xie Ting and Secretariat Courier Xu Ling as envoys north to open friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: That June he sent Jiankang magistrate Xie Ting and courier Xu Ling north to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 時侯景鎮壽春，疑懼，累啟請絕和，及致書與異餉金二百兩，又致書於制局監周石珍令具申聞。

translations.literal: At that time Hou Jing was garrisoned at Shouchun, suspicious and fearful; he repeatedly memorialized requesting that peace be broken off, and also sent a letter to Yi with two hundred liang of gold as a gift; he further sent a letter to Bureau Commissioner Zhou Shizhen ordering him to report fully to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, holding Shouchun, grew anxious. He repeatedly petitioned to break off the peace talks and wrote to Yi with two hundred liang of gold as a gift; he also wrote the bureau commissioner Zhou Shizhen demanding a full report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 異納其金而不停北使，景遂反。

translations.literal: Yi accepted his gold but did not stop the northern envoys; Jing thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took the gold but did not halt the northern mission—and Hou Jing rebelled.

sentences.zh: 初，景謀反，合州刺史鄱陽王范、司州刺史羊鴉仁並累有啟聞。

translations.literal: Initially, when Jing plotted rebellion, Governor of Hezhou the Prince of Poyang Fan and Governor of Sizhou Yang Yaren both repeatedly sent memorials reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing first plotted rebellion, Prince Fan of Poyang, governor of He province, and Yang Yaren, governor of Si province, both sent repeated warnings.

sentences.zh: 異以景孤立寄命，必不應爾，乃謂使曰：「鄱陽王遂不許國家有一客！

translations.literal: Yi, considering that Jing was isolated and had placed his life in others' hands, would surely not act thus, therefore said to the envoy: 'The Prince of Poyang thus will not allow the state to have even one guest!'
translations.idiomatic: Yi decided Hou Jing, isolated and dependent on Liang, would never dare rebel. He told the messenger, 'The Prince of Poyang won't even let the state keep one guest!'

sentences.zh: 」並不為聞奏。

translations.literal: And he did not memorialize any of it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He never forwarded their reports to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及賊至板橋，使前壽州司馬徐思玉先至求見於上，上召問之，思玉紿稱反賊，請閑陳事。

translations.literal: When the rebels reached Banqiao, he sent former Shouzhou Assistant Commander Xu Siyu ahead to request an audience with the Emperor; the Emperor summoned and questioned him; Siyu deceptively claimed to be a rebel and asked to state affairs privately.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels reached Banqiao, Hou Jing sent the former Shouzhou officer Xu Siyu ahead to request an audience. The emperor summoned him, and Siyu lied that he came from the rebels and asked to speak in private.

sentences.zh: 上將屏左右，舍人高善寶曰：「思玉從賊中來，情偽難測，安可使其獨在殿上。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to dismiss those around him; Gentleman Gao Shanbao said: 'Siyu came from among the rebels—the true and false are hard to measure; how can he be allowed alone on the palace hall?'
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to dismiss his attendants, attendant Gao Shanbao objected: 'Siyu came straight from the enemy camp—we can't know his true intent. How can we leave him alone with you in the hall?'

sentences.zh: 」時異侍坐，乃曰：「徐思玉豈是刺客邪？

translations.literal: At that time Yi was attending seated beside him, and said: 'Is Xu Siyu an assassin?'
translations.idiomatic: Yi, who was seated beside the emperor, said, 'Do you think Xu Siyu is an assassin?'

sentences.zh: 何言之僻。

translations.literal: How eccentric to speak thus.'
translations.idiomatic: What a strange thing to say.'

sentences.zh: 」善寶曰：「思玉已將臨賀入北，詎可輕信。

translations.literal: Shanbao said: 'Siyu has already taken Linhe north—how can he be lightly trusted?'
translations.idiomatic: Shanbao replied, 'Siyu already escorted Linhe to the north—how can we trust him lightly?'

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，思玉果出賊啟，異大慚。

translations.literal: Before the words ended, Siyu indeed produced the rebels' memorial; Yi was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking, Siyu produced Hou Jing's rebel manifesto—and Yi was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 賊遂以討異及陸驗為名。

translations.literal: The rebels thereupon took punishing Yi and Lu Yan as their rallying cry.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then marched under the banner of punishing Yi and Lu Yan.

sentences.zh: 及景至城下，又射啟言：「朱異等蔑弄朝權，輕作威福，臣為讒臣所陷，欲加屠戮。

translations.literal: When Jing reached below the walls, he again shot in a memorial saying: 'Zhu Yi and others scornfully play with court power and lightly wield authority and favor; your subject has been trapped by slanderous ministers who wish to add slaughter to it.'
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing reached the city walls, he shot a message inside: 'Zhu Yi and his faction mock the court's authority and abuse their power. Slandered by such men, I face slaughter.'

sentences.zh: 陛下誅異等，臣斂轡北歸」。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty executes Yi and the others, your subject will gather his reins and return north.'
translations.idiomatic: Execute Yi and his clique, Your Majesty, and I will pull in my reins and march north.'

sentences.zh: 帝問簡文曰：「有是乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Crown Prince Jianwen: 'Is there such a thing?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Crown Prince Jianwen, 'Is any of this true?'

translations.literal: He replied: 'It is so.'
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince answered, 'Yes.'

sentences.zh: 帝召有司將誅之，簡文曰：「賊特以異等為名耳，今日殺異，無救於急，適足貽笑將來。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned the relevant offices intending to execute him; Jianwen said: 'The rebels merely take Yi and the others as a name; to kill Yi today would not save the emergency—it would only be enough to leave a laugh for those to come.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called for Yi's execution. Jianwen argued: 'The rebels are using Yi only as a pretext. Killing him now won't help the crisis—it will only make us a laughingstock later.'

sentences.zh: 若祅氛既息，誅之未晚。

translations.literal: If the evil miasma has already ceased, executing him would not be too late.'
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion is over, it won't be too late to execute him.'

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 異之方幸，在朝莫不側目，雖皇太子亦不能平。

translations.literal: While Yi was at the height of favor, everyone at court looked askance; even the Crown Prince could not be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: While Yi basked in imperial favor, the whole court watched him with loathing—even the crown prince could barely contain his resentment.

sentences.zh: 至是城內咸尤異，簡文為四言湣亂詩曰：「湣彼阪田，嗟斯氛霧。

translations.literal: At this point everyone in the city blamed Yi; Jianwen composed a four-character 'Poem Mourning the Rebellion' saying: 'Alas, those sloping fields—lament this miasma and fog.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the whole city blamed Yi. Jianwen wrote a four-character poem mourning the upheaval: 'Alas for those terraced fields—what miasma and fog is this!'

sentences.zh: 謀之不臧，褰我王度。

translations.literal: Their planning was not good—it has drawn aside our royal measure.'
translations.idiomatic: Bad counsel has torn aside the royal standard.'

sentences.zh: 」又制圍城賦，末章云：「彼高冠及厚履，並鼎食而乘肥。

translations.literal: He also composed the 'Rhapsody on Besieged City,' whose final section says: 'Those high caps and thick-soled shoes—all eating from tripods and riding fat steeds.'
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the 'Rhapsody of the Besieged City,' whose closing lines run: 'Those high caps and thick shoes—all feasting from cauldrons, all riding fat horses.'

sentences.zh: 升紫霄之丹地，排玉殿之金扉。

translations.literal: Ascending the cinnabar ground of the Purple Heights, pushing open the golden doors of the jade halls.'
translations.idiomatic: They mount the crimson floor of the purple palace and push open the gilt doors of the jade halls.'

sentences.zh: 陳謀謨之啟沃，宣政刑之福威。

translations.literal: Expounding counsel and strategy to pour out nourishment; proclaiming governance and punishments, blessing and might.'
translations.idiomatic: They pour out counsel at the emperor's side and wield the blessings and terrors of law and government.'

sentences.zh: 四郊以之多壘，萬邦以之未綏。

translations.literal: The four suburbs because of them have many ramparts; the myriad states because of them are not yet pacified.'
translations.idiomatic: Their cities bristle with ramparts on every side; the realm remains unsettled.'

sentences.zh: 問豺狼其何者？

translations.literal: Ask—which are the wolves and jackals?
translations.idiomatic: Who are the wolves?

sentences.zh: 訪虺蜴之為誰？

translations.literal: Inquire—who are the venomous snakes and lizards?
translations.idiomatic: Who are the vipers?

sentences.zh: 」並以指異。

translations.literal: All were pointing at Yi.
translations.idiomatic: All of it was aimed at Yi.

sentences.zh: 又帝登南樓望賊，顧謂異曰：「四郊多壘，誰之罪歟？

translations.literal: Also, the Emperor ascended the South Tower to look at the rebels, turned and said to Yi: 'The four suburbs have many ramparts—whose crime is it?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor climbed the South Tower to look at the rebel host and turned to Yi: 'The Analects say many ramparts in the suburbs—whose fault is this?'

sentences.zh: 」異流汗不能對。

translations.literal: Yi sweated but could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi broke out in sweat and could not reply.

sentences.zh: 慚憤發病卒，時年六十七。

translations.literal: Ashamed and indignant, he fell ill and died; he was sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with shame and rage, he fell ill and died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 詔贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Vice Minister of the Interior, Right.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him vice minister of the right.

sentences.zh: 舊尚書官不以為贈，及異卒，武帝悼惜之，方議贈事，左右有善異者，乃啟曰：「異生平所懷，願得執法。

translations.literal: By old rule, Minister of the Interior posts were not used for posthumous grants; when Yi died, Emperor Wu mourned and regretted it, and was just deliberating the posthumous grant when someone around him who favored Yi memorialized: 'In life what Yi harbored in his heart was a wish to hold the law.'
translations.idiomatic: By custom, ministerial posts were not given as posthumous honors. When Yi died the emperor mourned him and was deciding what title to grant when a courtier who favored Yi reported: 'All his life Yi wished to serve as a law officer.'

sentences.zh: 」帝因其宿志，特有此贈。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because of his longstanding wish, specially granted this posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring that lifelong wish, the emperor specially granted the vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 異居權要三十餘年，善承上旨，故特被寵任。

translations.literal: Yi occupied a position of power for more than thirty years, good at receiving the sovereign's intent, hence he was specially entrusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Yi held power for more than thirty years, skilled at catching the emperor's mood, and for that reason enjoyed special trust.

sentences.zh: 曆官自員外常侍至侍中，四官皆珥貂，自右衛率至領軍，四職並驅鹵簿，近代未之有也。

translations.literal: In offices he passed from External Member Attendant Cavalier to Palace Attendant—four posts all wearing the pendant fox-tail ear ornament; from Right Commandant of the Guard to Army Commander—four posts all driving the guard of honor—nothing like it in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: From external attendant through palace attendant, he held four offices that entitled him to wear the court insignia; from right guard commandant through army commander, four posts that entitled him to a full guard procession—unprecedented in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 異及諸子自潮溝列宅至青溪，其中有台池翫好，每暇日與賓客遊焉。

translations.literal: Yi and his sons had a row of residences from Chaogou to Qingxi; among them were terraces, ponds, and pleasures; on each day of leisure they roamed them with guests.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his sons owned a stretch of mansions from Chaogou to Qingxi, with pavilions and ponds for pleasure; on free days they entertained guests there.

sentences.zh: 四方饋遺，財貨充積，性吝嗇，未嘗有散施。

translations.literal: Gifts from the four directions—wealth and goods piled full; by nature stingy and miserly, he never once distributed or gave away.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts from everywhere piled up his stores of wealth, yet he was miserly and never gave anything away.

sentences.zh: 廚下珍羞恒腐爛，每月常棄十數車，雖諸子別房亦不分贍。

translations.literal: Delicacies in the kitchen constantly rotted; every month he routinely discarded ten-odd cartloads; even to his sons in separate households he did not divide provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Delicacies spoiled in his kitchens by the cartload every month, and he would not even share food with his sons in other households.

sentences.zh: 所撰禮、易講疏及儀注文集百餘篇。

translations.literal: What he authored: commentaries on the Rituals and Changes, and a collected corpus of ritual regulations—in all more than a hundred chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than a hundred works, including commentaries on the Rituals and the Changes and numerous ritual manuals.

sentences.zh: 子肅，位國子博士；

translations.literal: His son Su held the position of Erudite of the National University;
translations.idiomatic: His son Su became a National University erudite;

sentences.zh: 次閏，司徒掾。

translations.literal: The next, Run, was an aide on the Minister of Education's staff.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Run, was a staff officer under the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 並遇亂卒。

translations.literal: Both encountered chaos and died.
translations.idiomatic: Both perished in the upheaval.

sentences.zh: 顧協字正禮，吳郡吳人，晉司空和六世孫也。

translations.literal: Gu Xie, style name Zhengli, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery—the sixth-generation descendant of He, Grand Minister of Works of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xie, courtesy name Zhengli, came from Wu in Wu commandery and was a sixth-generation descendant of the Jin grand minister He.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，隨母養於外氏。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he followed his mother and was reared at his maternal family's house.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father early and grew up in his mother's family home.

sentences.zh: 外從祖右光祿大夫張永嘗攜內外孫侄游虎丘山，拹年數歲，永撫之曰：「兒欲何戲？

translations.literal: His maternal great-uncle, Right Grand Master of Bright Feasts Zhang Yong, once took his inner and outer grandchildren and nephews to tour Tiger Hill; Xie was several years old. Yong stroked him and said: 'My child, what game would you like?'
translations.idiomatic: His maternal great-uncle Zhang Yong, Right Grand Master of Bright Feasts, once took the family's grandchildren and nephews to Tiger Hill. Gu Xie was only a few years old. Yong patted his head and asked, 'What would you like to play, boy?'

sentences.zh: 」協曰：「兒政欲枕石漱流。

translations.literal: Xie said: 'Your child truly wishes to pillow upon stone and rinse the mouth in flowing streams.'
translations.idiomatic: Xie answered, 'I would rather use a rock for a pillow and rinse my mouth in a mountain stream.'

sentences.zh: 」永歎息曰：「顧氏興於此子。

translations.literal: Yong sighed and said: 'The Gu clan will rise through this child.'
translations.idiomatic: Yong sighed and said, 'The Gu family will flourish because of this boy.'

sentences.zh: 」及長好學，以精力稱。

translations.literal: When he grew up he loved learning and was known for vigor and industry.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he devoted himself to learning and was admired for his tireless energy.

sentences.zh: 外氏諸張多賢達，有識鑒，內弟率尤推重焉。

translations.literal: Among his maternal family many of the Zhangs were worthy and accomplished, with judgment and insight; his younger maternal cousin Shuai especially esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the Zhangs on his mother's side were talented men of discernment, and his cousin Zhang Shuai held him in special regard.

sentences.zh: 初為揚州議曹從事，舉秀才。

translations.literal: At first he served as staff member of the deliberation section in Yang province and was nominated as a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a staff officer in Yang province's deliberation office and passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 尚書令沈約覽其策而歎曰：「江左以來，未有斯作。

translations.literal: Minister of the Interior Shen Yue read his examination essay and sighed, saying: 'Since the lands east of the Yangtze, there has never been writing like this.'
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Shen Yue read his examination essay, he marveled: 'Since the Eastern Jin came south, nothing like this has been written.'

sentences.zh: 」為兼廷尉正。

translations.literal: He was appointed concurrent chief judge of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was made concurrent chief judge of the court of justice.

sentences.zh: 太尉臨川王聞其名，召掌書記，仍侍西豐侯正德讀。

translations.literal: Grand Commander the Prince of Linchuan heard his reputation, summoned him to manage records, and had him attend on the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, for study.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Linchuan, serving as grand commander, heard of him, appointed him to handle records, and had him tutor the Marquis of Xifeng, Xiao Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 正德為巴西、梓潼郡，協除所部新安令。

translations.literal: When Zhengde governed Ba and Zitong commanderies, Xie was appointed magistrate of Xin'an under his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengde took charge of Ba and Zitong, Xie was appointed magistrate of Xin'an in his domain.

sentences.zh: 未至縣遭母憂，刺史始興王厚資遣之，送喪還。

translations.literal: Before reaching the county he suffered his mother's death; the Governor, the Prince of Shixing, generously funded his journey and sent him back to convey the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached the county his mother died. The Prince of Shixing, the provincial governor, gave him generous support to escort the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 于峽江遇風，同旅皆漂溺，唯協一舫觸石得泊焉。

translations.literal: On the Yangtze gorges he encountered wind; all fellow travelers were swept away and drowned—only Xie's single boat struck a rock and was able to moor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yangtze gorges a storm struck. Every other boat in the convoy was swept under; only Xie's vessel struck a rock and held fast.

sentences.zh: 咸謂精誠所致。

translations.literal: All said this was caused by the power of his sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone took this as proof of his heartfelt devotion.

sentences.zh: 張率嘗薦之於帝，問協年，率言三十有五。

translations.literal: Zhang Shuai once recommended him to the Emperor; the Emperor asked Xie's age, and Shuai said thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuai once recommended him to the emperor, who asked Xie's age. Shuai replied that he was thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「北方高涼，四十強仕，南方卑濕，三十已衰。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'The north is lofty and cool—at forty one is in vigorous service; the south is low and damp—at thirty one is already in decline.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'The north is high and cool, and men there are still vigorous at forty; the south is low and damp, and by thirty they are already fading.'

sentences.zh: 如協便為已老，但其事親孝，與友信，亦不可遺於草澤。

translations.literal: Someone like Xie would already be considered old, yet in serving his parents he is filial and with friends he is trustworthy—such a man cannot be abandoned to the wilderness.'
translations.idiomatic: By that measure Xie is already old, but he is filial to his parents and faithful to his friends. A man like that must not be left to rust in the wilds.'

sentences.zh: 卿便稱敕喚出。

translations.literal: You may announce by edict and summon him forth.'
translations.idiomatic: Announce my order and summon him.'

sentences.zh: 」於是以協為兼太學博士。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xie was appointed concurrent Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was then appointed concurrent academy erudite.

sentences.zh: 累遷湘東王參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to aide to the Prince of Xiangdong, concurrently recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as aide to the Prince of Xiangdong and recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 普通中，有詔舉士，湘東王表薦之，即召拜通直散騎侍郎，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: During the Putong era an edict was issued to recommend scholars; the Prince of Xiangdong memorialized and recommended him, and he was at once summoned and appointed Palace Courier and Concurrent Secretariat Attendant for Imperial Communications.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putong era, when the throne called for recommended scholars, the Prince of Xiangdong nominated him. He was summoned at once and appointed palace courier and concurrent secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 大通三年，霆擊大航華表然盡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, lightning struck the ceremonial column on the Great Bridge and burned it completely.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 3, lightning struck the ornamental column on the Great Bridge and burned it to ashes.

sentences.zh: 建康縣馳啟，協以為非吉祥，未即呈聞。

translations.literal: The Jiankang county office sent an urgent report; Xie considered it inauspicious and did not immediately present it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang county sent an urgent report, but Xie judged the omen unlucky and withheld it from the throne.

sentences.zh: 後帝知之，曰：「霆之所擊，一本罰惡龍，二彰朕之有過。

translations.literal: Later when the Emperor learned of it, he said: 'Where thunder strikes, on the one hand it punishes evil dragons; on the other it manifests that I have faults.'
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later learned of it, he said, 'Thunder strikes first to punish evil dragons and second to reveal my own failings.'

sentences.zh: 協掩惡揚善，非曰忠公。

translations.literal: Xie hid the bad and proclaimed the good—this cannot be called loyal and upright.'
translations.idiomatic: Xie covered up ill omens and reported only good news—that is not loyal service.'

sentences.zh: 」由是見免。

translations.literal: Because of this he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 後守鴻臚卿，員外散騎常侍，卿、舍人並如故。

translations.literal: Later he served as Chief Minister of Guest Affairs and External Attendant Cavalier, while his posts as chief minister and attendant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief minister of guest affairs and external attendant cavalier, retaining his attendant duties.

sentences.zh: 自為近臣，便繁幾密，每有述制，敕前示協，時輩榮之。

translations.literal: Since becoming a close attendant, he handled frequent and confidential matters; whenever there was a proclamation to draft, the Emperor would show it to Xie beforehand—men of the age counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: As a close attendant he handled dense, confidential work. Whenever an edict was drafted, the emperor showed it to Xie first—a mark of honor his peers envied.

sentences.zh: 卒官無衾以斂，為士子所嗟歎。

translations.literal: When he died in office there was no quilt to wrap his body for burial—the scholars lamented this.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office without even a quilt to wrap his body for burial, and scholars mourned the fact.

sentences.zh: 武帝悼惜之，為舉哀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu mourned and regretted it, and held mourning rites for him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu grieved for him and ordered mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍，諡曰溫子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Attendant Cavalier, with posthumous name Wenzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made attendant cavalier with the posthumous name Wenzi.

sentences.zh: 協少清介，有志操，初為廷尉正，冬服單薄，寺卿蔡法度欲解襦與之，憚其清嚴，不敢發口，謂人曰：「我願解身上襦與顧郎，顧郎難衣食者。

translations.literal: Xie from youth was pure and upright, with lofty ambitions; when he first served as chief judge of the Court of Justice, his winter clothing was thin; the chief minister Cai Fadu wished to take off his jacket and give it to him, but feared his austere severity and dared not speak up, saying to others: 'I wish to take off the jacket on my body and give it to Gentleman Gu, but Gentleman Gu is difficult—regarding food and clothing.'
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xie was incorruptible and high-minded. When he first served as chief judge of the court of justice, his winter clothes were thin. Chief Minister Cai Fadu wanted to lend him his own jacket but feared Xie's stern integrity and could not bring himself to offer it. He told others, 'I'd gladly give Gu my coat, but he won't accept food or clothing from anyone.'

sentences.zh: 」竟不敢以遺之。

translations.literal: In the end he dared not give it to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he never did.

sentences.zh: 及為舍人，同官者皆潤屋，協在省十六載，器服飲食不改于常。

translations.literal: When he became an attendant, all his colleagues enriched their houses, but Xie throughout sixteen years in the bureau—his vessels, clothing, food and drink did not change from the usual.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became an attendant, his colleagues all grew rich, yet through sixteen years in the secretariat Xie's utensils, dress, food, and drink never changed.

sentences.zh: 有門生始來事協，知其廉潔，不敢厚餉，止送錢二千，協發怒，杖二十，因此事者絕於饋遺。

translations.literal: A student retainer had just come to serve Xie, knowing his integrity and purity, dared not give a lavish gift, and sent only two thousand cash; Xie grew angry and had him beaten twenty strokes; because of this, those who wished to give gifts ceased entirely.
translations.idiomatic: A new student attendant, knowing Xie's probity, dared not offer a lavish gift and sent only two thousand cash. Xie flew into a rage and had him beaten twenty strokes. After that, gift-giving stopped entirely.

sentences.zh: 自丁艱憂，遂終身布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: From the time he completed mourning for his mother, for the rest of his life he wore plain cloth and ate simple vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he wore plain cloth and ate simple food for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 少時將娉舅息女，未成昏而協母亡，免喪後不復娶。

translations.literal: In youth he was about to marry his maternal cousin's daughter; before the marriage was completed Xie's mother died; after mourning he never remarried.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was betrothed to his cousin's daughter, but his mother died before the wedding. After mourning he never took another wife.

sentences.zh: 年六十餘，此女猶未他適，協義而迎之。

translations.literal: When he was over sixty, this woman still had not married another; Xie out of righteousness went and received her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When he was past sixty she was still unmarried. Out of duty Xie went and took her as his wife.

sentences.zh: 晚雖判合，卒無胤嗣。

translations.literal: Though they united late in life, in the end he had no heir.
translations.idiomatic: They married late in life, but he left no children.

sentences.zh: 協博極群書，於文字及禽獸草木尤稱精詳，撰異姓苑五卷，瑣語十卷，文集十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: Xie exhaustively mastered all books; in graphs and characters and in birds, beasts, plants and trees he was especially praised for meticulous knowledge; he compiled Records of Heterogeneous Surnames in five fascicles, Petty Talk in ten fascicles, and a collected corpus in ten fascicles—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xie mastered an enormous library of texts and was especially renowned for his knowledge of writing and of birds, beasts, plants, and trees. He compiled Records of Heterogeneous Surnames in five fascicles, Petty Talk in ten fascicles, and a collected works in ten fascicles, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 徐摛字士秀，東海郯人也，一字士繢。

translations.literal: Xu Chi, style name Shiqiu, was a man of Tan in Donghai—also styled Shihui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chi, courtesy name Shiqiu, came from Tan in Donghai commandery; he also used the courtesy name Shihui.

sentences.zh: 祖憑道，宋海陵太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Pingdao was Governor of Hailing under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pingdao served as governor of Hailing under the Liu-Song.

sentences.zh: 父超之，梁天監初位員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His father Chaozhi, in the early Tianjian era of Liang, held the post of External Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chaozhi held the post of external attendant cavalier in the early Liang reign era Tianjian.

sentences.zh: 摛幼好學，及長，遍覽經史，屬文好為新變，不拘舊體。

translations.literal: From childhood Chi loved learning; when grown he read extensively in the classics and histories, and in composing texts he favored new forms of change, not bound by old conventions.
translations.idiomatic: Chi loved learning from childhood. As an adult he read widely in the classics and histories and wrote in a fresh, innovative style unbound by older forms.

sentences.zh: 晉安王綱出戍石頭，武帝謂周舍曰：「為我求一人，文學俱長，兼有行者，欲令與晉安遊處。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin'an Gang went out to garrison Shitou, Emperor Wu said to Zhou She: 'Find a man for me—equal in letters and scholarship, who also has conduct—whom I wish to have keep Jin'an company in study and leisure.'
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiao Gang of Jin'an went out to garrison Shitou, Emperor Wu told Zhou She, 'Find me someone equally strong in letters and learning, with good character, to keep Jin'an company.'

sentences.zh: 」舍曰：「臣外弟徐摛，形質陋小，若不勝衣，而堪此選。

translations.literal: She said: 'My maternal cousin Xu Chi—his form and quality are ugly and small, as if unable to fill out his clothes—yet he is fit for this selection.'
translations.idiomatic: She replied, 'My cousin Xu Chi is small and unprepossessing—he looks as though his clothes might swallow him—but he is the man for this.'

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「必有仲宣之才，亦不簡貌。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Surely he has the talent of Wang Can; then one does not pick by appearance.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'If he has Wang Can's talent, appearance hardly matters.'

sentences.zh: 」乃以摛為侍讀。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chi was appointed Study Companion.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was appointed study companion.

sentences.zh: 大通初，王總戎北侵，以摛兼寧蠻府長史，參贊戎政，教命軍書，多自摛出。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, when the Prince commanded troops on the northern campaign, he made Chi concurrent Chief Secretary of the Pacification Office, assisting in military affairs; military orders and proclamations mostly issued from Chi.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Datong era, when the prince led a northern campaign, he made Chi chief secretary of the pacification office. Chi helped direct military affairs, and most orders and dispatches came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 王入為皇太子，轉家令，兼管記，尋帶領直。

translations.literal: When the Prince entered court as Crown Prince, Chi was transferred to Chief of the Household and concurrently directed the record, soon also holding command of the immediate guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Chi was made chief of the household and head recorder, and soon also commanded the immediate guard.

sentences.zh: 摛文體既別，春坊盡學之，「宮體」之號，自斯而始。

translations.literal: Since Chi's literary style was distinctive, the Eastern Palace all studied it—the title 'Palace Style' began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chi's literary style was distinctive, the whole Eastern Palace took it up—the name 'Palace Style' dates from this.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之怒，召摛將加誚責，及見，應對明敏，辭義可觀，乃意釋。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of it in anger and summoned Chi intending to reprimand and punish him; when he saw him, Chi answered with clarity and quickness, his rhetoric and argument worth viewing—the Emperor's intent was released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it and angrily summoned Chi to rebuke him. But when they met, Chi answered with sharp clarity and compelling eloquence, and the emperor's anger dissolved.

sentences.zh: 因問五經大義，次問歷代史及百家雜記，末論釋教。

translations.literal: Thereupon he questioned him on the great meaning of the Five Classics, next on dynastic histories and the miscellaneous records of the hundred schools, and finally on Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: He then tested Chi on the Five Classics, then on dynastic history and the writings of the hundred schools, and finally on Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 摛商較從橫，應答如響，帝甚加歎異，更被親狎，寵遇日隆。

translations.literal: Chi debated back and forth with agility, answering like an echo; the Emperor greatly marveled and showed special astonishment, treated him with greater intimacy, and favor daily grew.
translations.idiomatic: Chi debated with ease and answered like an echo. The emperor was astonished, drew him closer, and favored him more each day.

sentences.zh: 領軍朱異不悅，謂所親曰：「徐叟出入兩宮，漸來見逼，我須早為之所。

translations.literal: Army Commander Zhu Yi was displeased and said to those close to him: 'Old Xu goes in and out of the two palaces and is increasingly pressing on me—I must deal with him early.'
translations.idiomatic: Army Commander Zhu Yi was displeased and told his intimates, 'Old Xu shuttles between the two palaces and is crowding me out. I need to move against him soon.'

sentences.zh: 」遂承閑白帝曰：「摛年老，又愛泉石，意在一郡自養。

translations.literal: He then seized an opportunity and reported to the Emperor: 'Chi is old, and moreover loves springs and rocks—his mind is set on governing one commandery to nurture himself.'
translations.idiomatic: He seized a chance and told the emperor, 'Chi is getting old and loves mountains and streams. What he really wants is a quiet commandery where he can retire.'

sentences.zh: 」帝謂摛欲之，乃召摛曰：「新安大好山水，任昉等並經為之，卿為我臨此郡。

translations.literal: The Emperor thought Chi wanted this and thereupon summoned Chi and said: 'Xin'an has excellent mountains and waters; Ren Fang and others all served there—go govern that commandery for me.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Chi wanted exactly that and summoned him. 'Xin'an has splendid scenery,' he said. 'Ren Fang and others all served there. Go govern it for me.'

sentences.zh: 」中大通三年，遂出為新安太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong he was sent out as Governor of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong year 3 he was sent out as governor of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，教人禮義，勸課農桑，期月風俗便改。

translations.literal: His government was pure and quiet; he taught people ritual propriety and urged the farming of mulberry trees and grain—in the space of a month local custom was changed.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was quiet and upright. He taught ritual propriety, encouraged mulberry planting and farming, and within a month local customs changed.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，為中庶子。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was made Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was made junior mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時臨城公納夫人王氏，即簡文妃侄女。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Lincheng was taking a wife from the Wang clan—the niece of Crown Prince Jianwen's consort.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Lincheng was marrying a woman of the Wang clan, a niece of Crown Prince Jianwen's consort.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋以來，初昏三日，婦見舅姑，眾賓皆列觀，引春秋義云：「丁丑，夫人姜氏至。

translations.literal: Since Jin and Song, on the third day after the first marriage the wife sees her father-in-law and mother-in-law and all guests are arrayed to observe; they cited the Spring and Autumn meaning: 'On dingchou the lady Jiang arrived.'
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin and Song times, on the third day after a wedding the bride would be presented to her parents-in-law while guests looked on. Ritual officers cited the Spring and Autumn Annals: 'On dingchou the lady Jiang arrived.'

sentences.zh: 戊寅，公使大夫宗婦覿用幣」。

translations.literal: On wuyin the Duke sent the grand officer and the chief wife of the clan to meet her with silken gifts.'
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the duke sent the grand officer and the chief wife of the clan to greet her with silken gifts.'

sentences.zh: 戊寅即丁丑之明日，故禮官據此皆云：「宜依舊觀」。

translations.literal: Wuyin is the day after dingchou; therefore the ritual officers relying on this all said: 'It is proper to follow the old observance.'
translations.idiomatic: Since wuyin is the day after dingchou, the ritual officers argued that the old public viewing should be followed.'

sentences.zh: 簡文問摛，摛議曰：「儀禮云：'質明贊見婦于舅姑。

translations.literal: Jianwen asked Chi; Chi deliberated, saying: 'The Ceremonies say: "At dawn the sponsor presents the wife to the father-in-law and mother-in-law."'
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen asked Chi for his view. Chi argued: 'The Ceremonies say, "At dawn the sponsor presents the bride to her parents-in-law."'

sentences.zh: '雜記又云：'婦見舅姑，兄弟姊妹皆立于堂下。

translations.literal: The Miscellaneous Records also say: 'When the wife sees father-in-law and mother-in-law, brothers and sisters all stand below the hall.'
translations.idiomatic: The Miscellaneous Records add, "When the bride is presented, brothers and sisters stand below the hall."'

sentences.zh: '政言婦是外宗，未審澗令，所以舅延外客，姑率內賓，堂下之儀，以備盛禮。

translations.literal: This means the wife is of an outside lineage, not yet versed in the rules of the inner quarters—therefore the father-in-law receives outside guests and the mother-in-law leads inner guests; the ceremony below the hall is to complete the full rites.
translations.idiomatic: This refers to a bride from an outside clan who does not yet know the rules of the inner household. The father-in-law receives outside guests and the mother-in-law leads inner guests; the hall ceremony completes the full rite.

sentences.zh: 近代婦于舅姑本有戚屬，不相瞻者。

translations.literal: In recent times between wife and in-laws there were originally family ties, so they did not regard each other.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times brides and in-laws were often already related and did not need such a formal presentation.

sentences.zh: 夫人乃妃侄女，有異他姻，覿見之儀，謂應可略。

translations.literal: This lady is the consort's niece, different from other affinal connections; the ritual of formal meeting, it is said, should be abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: This bride is the consort's niece, a closer tie than ordinary marriage. The formal viewing, I believe, may be omitted.

sentences.zh: 」簡文從其議。

translations.literal: Jianwen followed his deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 除太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left commandant of the crown prince's guard.

sentences.zh: 及侯景攻陷台城，時簡文居永福省。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing captured Taicheng, at that time Jianwen resided in Yongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing stormed Taicheng, Jianwen was living in Yongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 賊眾奔入，侍衛走散，莫有存者。

translations.literal: The rebel host rushed in; guards and attendants fled and scattered—not one remained.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel troops poured in. Guards and attendants fled until none remained.

sentences.zh: 摛獨侍立不動，徐謂景曰：「侯公當以禮見，何得如此。

translations.literal: Chi alone stood attending without moving, and slowly said to Jing: 'Lord Hou should be received with ritual propriety—how can it be like this?'
translations.idiomatic: Chi alone stood his ground and calmly told Hou Jing, 'Lord Hou, you should be received with proper ceremony. What is this?'

sentences.zh: 」凶威遂折，侯景乃拜。

translations.literal: His fierce authority thereupon bent, and Hou Jing then performed obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's swagger broke, and he bowed.

sentences.zh: 由是常憚摛。

translations.literal: Because of this he always feared Chi.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he always feared Chi.

sentences.zh: 簡文嗣位，進授左衛將軍，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: When Jianwen succeeded to the throne, he was promoted and granted Left Guard General, but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianwen ascended the throne, Chi was promoted to left guard general, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 簡文被閉，摛不獲朝謁，因感氣疾而卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: Jianwen was confined; Chi could not gain audience at court, and consequently, afflicted by breath illness, died—he was seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen was confined, and Chi could no longer attend court. Grief and indignation brought on a fatal illness, and he died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、太子詹事，諡貞子。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince, posthumous name Zhenzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and grand mentor to the crown prince, with the posthumous name Zhenzi.

sentences.zh: 長子陵，最知名。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ling was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ling became the most famous.

sentences.zh: 陵字孝穆。

translations.literal: Ling's style name was Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's courtesy name was Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 母臧氏，嘗夢五色雲化為鳳，集左肩上，已而誕陵。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Zang, once dreamed that five-colored clouds transformed into a phoenix and alighted on her left shoulder; not long after Ling was born.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zang, dreamed that five-colored clouds turned into a phoenix and settled on her left shoulder. Soon after, Ling was born.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，家人攜以候沙門釋寶志，寶志摩其頂曰：「天上石麒麟也。

translations.literal: When he was several years old the family took him to wait on the monk Baozhi, who rubbed his crown and said: 'A stone qilin from heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: When he was a few years old the family took him to the monk Baozhi, who rubbed his head and said, 'A stone qilin sent from heaven.'

sentences.zh: 」光宅寺慧雲法師每嗟陵早就，謂之顏回。

translations.literal: Huiyun, Dharma Master of Guangzai Temple, always sighed that Ling matured early, calling him Yan Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyun, the dharma master of Guangzai Temple, always marveled at Ling's precocity and called him a Yan Hui.

sentences.zh: 八歲屬文，十三通莊、老義。

translations.literal: At eight he composed texts; at thirteen he thoroughly penetrated Zhuangzi and Laozi meanings.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he was already writing; at thirteen he had mastered the Zhuangzi and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 及長，博涉史籍，從橫有口辯。

translations.literal: When grown he broadly traversed historical records and had resourceful eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he ranged widely through history and was a nimble debater.

sentences.zh: 父摛為晉安王諮議，王又引陵參寧蠻府軍事。

translations.literal: His father Chi was Counselor of the Prince of Jin'an, and the Prince also recruited Ling as staff member on the Pacification Office military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi served as counselor to the Prince of Jin'an, and the prince also recruited Ling as a staff officer in the pacification office.

sentences.zh: 王立為皇太子，東宮置學士，陵充其選。

translations.literal: When the Prince was established as Crown Prince, the Eastern Palace established Academicians—Ling filled one of the selections.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, the Eastern Palace formed a corps of academicians, and Ling was chosen among them.

sentences.zh: 稍遷尚書度支郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Lang of the Revenue Section of the Ministry of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to a post in the ministry's revenue section.

sentences.zh: 出為上虞令。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞劉孝儀與陵先有隙，風聞劾陵在縣贓汙，因坐免。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiaoyi and Ling had an old grudge; on rumor and report he impeached Ling for corruption while in the county, and Ling was dismissed from office because of it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiaoyi, who bore an old grudge against Ling, impeached him on rumor for corruption as magistrate, and Ling was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，為通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Palace Courier.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored as palace courier.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文在東宮，撰長春殿義記，使陵為序。

translations.literal: When Liang Crown Prince Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace he compiled Records of the Meaning of the Eternal Spring Hall and had Ling write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: While Crown Prince Jianwen was in the Eastern Palace, he compiled Records of the Meaning of the Eternal Spring Hall and had Ling write the preface.

sentences.zh: 又令于少傅府述己所制莊子義。

translations.literal: He also had him expound at the Junior Tutor's office the Zhuangzi meanings he himself had composed.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Ling lecture at the junior tutor's office on the Zhuangzi commentaries he himself had written.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，兼通直散騎常侍使魏，魏人授館宴賓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was concurrently External Attendant Cavalier as envoy to Wei; the Wei people lodged them and feasted the guests.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing year 2 he served concurrently as external attendant cavalier on a mission to Wei. The Wei hosts lodged the envoys and held a banquet.

sentences.zh: 是日甚熱，其主客魏收嘲陵曰：「今日之熱，當由徐常侍來。

translations.literal: That day was extremely hot; the chief host Wei Shou mocked Ling, saying: 'Today's heat must be because Attendant Xu has come.'
translations.idiomatic: The day was sweltering. The chief host Wei Shou teased Ling: 'This heat must be because Attendant Xu has arrived.'

sentences.zh: 」陵即答曰：「昔王肅至此，為魏始制禮儀；

translations.literal: Ling at once replied: 'In former times when Wang Su came here, Wei for the first time established ritual propriety;'
translations.idiomatic: Ling shot back, 'When Wang Su came here long ago, Wei learned ritual propriety for the first time;'

sentences.zh: 今我來聘，使卿復知寒暑。

translations.literal: Now that I have come on a mission, I make you once again know cold and heat.'
translations.idiomatic: now that I have come on a mission, I shall teach you once again to distinguish cold from heat.'

sentences.zh: 」收大慚。

translations.literal: Shou was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄為相，以收失言，囚之累日。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang of Qi was Chancellor, because Shou had misspoken, they imprisoned Ling for many days.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng, Wenxiang of Northern Qi, served as chancellor, Wei Shou's slip of the tongue led to Xu Ling's imprisonment for many days.

sentences.zh: 及侯景入寇，陵父摛先在圍城之內，陵不奉家信，便蔬食布衣，若居哀恤。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing invaded, Ling's father Chi was first inside the besieged city; Ling received no letters from his family, and so ate plain vegetables and wore coarse cloth, as though dwelling in mourning grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing invaded, Xu Ling's father Xu Chi was trapped inside the besieged capital. Receiving no word from home, Ling ate only plain food and wore coarse cloth, as though in mourning.

sentences.zh: 會齊受魏禪，梁元帝承制於江陵，復通使于齊。

translations.literal: Just then Qi received Wei's abdication, and Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional rule at Jiangling, and once again exchanged envoys with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Northern Qi received the Wei abdication, while Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed provisional rule at Jiangling and resumed diplomatic exchanges with Qi.

sentences.zh: 陵累求復命，終拘留不遣，乃致書于僕射楊遵彥，不報。

translations.literal: Ling repeatedly asked to return and report, but in the end was detained and not sent back; thereupon he wrote to Vice Director Yang Zunyan, and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling repeatedly petitioned to return home and report, but was detained and never sent back. He then wrote to Vice Director Yang Zunyan and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 及魏平江陵，齊送貞陽侯明為梁嗣，乃遣陵隨還。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jiangling, Qi sent the Marquis of Zhenyang, Ming, as successor to Liang, and then sent Ling to return with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei forces captured Jiangling, Northern Qi sent the Marquis of Zhenyang, Xiao Ming, to succeed the Liang throne and dispatched Xu Ling to return with him.

sentences.zh: 太尉王僧辯初拒境不納，明往復致書，皆陵辭也。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian at first refused at the border and would not admit him; Ming sent letters back and forth—all the phrasing was Ling's.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Wang Sengbian at first refused to admit them at the border. The letters Xiao Ming exchanged in the negotiations were all drafted by Xu Ling.

sentences.zh: 及明入，僧辯得陵大喜，以為尚書吏部郎，兼掌詔誥。

translations.literal: When Ming entered, Sengbian, having gotten Ling, was greatly delighted, and appointed him Lang of the Personnel Section of the Ministry of the Interior, concurrently in charge of edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiao Ming was admitted, Wang Sengbian was overjoyed to have Xu Ling and appointed him director of the Ministry of Personnel, with concurrent charge of imperial edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 其年陳武帝誅僧辯，仍進討韋載，而任約、徐嗣徽乘虛襲石頭，陵感僧辯舊恩，往赴約。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Wu of Chen executed Sengbian and continued advancing to attack Wei Zai; meanwhile Ren Yue and Xu Sihui seized the moment of vulnerability to assault Shitou. Ling, grateful for Sengbian's old kindness, went to join Yue.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Emperor Wu of Chen executed Wang Sengbian and pressed on against Wei Zai, while Ren Yue and Xu Sihui seized the opening to attack Shitou. Grateful for Sengbian's past kindness, Xu Ling went to join Ren Yue.

sentences.zh: 約平，武帝釋陵不問，以為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Yue was pacified, Emperor Wu released Ling without inquiry and appointed him Left Assistant Director of the Ministry of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: After Ren Yue was defeated, Emperor Wu pardoned Xu Ling without further inquiry and appointed him left assistant director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 紹泰二年，又使齊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaotai, he was again sent to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaotai, he was again sent on a mission to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 還除給事黃門侍郎，秘書監。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate and director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陳受禪，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Chen received the abdication, he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen dynasty was established, he was additionally made regular attendant of the fast cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天嘉四年，為五兵尚書，領大著作。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjia, he became Minister of the Five Weapons, concurrently heading the Grand Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianjia, he became minister of war and concurrently headed the imperial historiography office.

sentences.zh: 六年，除散騎常侍，御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was appointed regular attendant of the fast cavalry and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時安成王頊為司空，以帝弟之尊，權傾朝野。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Ancheng Xu was Minister of Works; by virtue of his rank as the emperor's younger brother, his power overshadowed the court and the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Xu of Ancheng served as minister of works, and by virtue of his status as the emperor's younger brother his power overshadowed the entire court.

sentences.zh: 直兵鮑僧叡假王威風，抑塞辭訟，大臣莫敢言，陵乃奏彈之。

translations.literal: Duty officer Bao Sengrui borrowed the prince's august prestige to obstruct and block legal petitions; none of the great ministers dared speak, so Ling memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's duty officer Bao Sengrui abused the prince's authority to block lawsuits, and none of the senior ministers dared speak out. Xu Ling thereupon memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 文帝見陵服章嚴肅，若不可犯，為斂容正坐。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen saw Ling's robes and insignia stern and solemn, as though not to be violated, and composed his expression and sat upright.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen saw Xu Ling in his official robes, stern and imposing as though not to be challenged, and composed his expression and sat upright.

sentences.zh: 陵進讀奏狀，時安成王殿上侍立，仰視文帝，流汗失色，陵遣殿中郎引王下殿。

translations.literal: Ling advanced and read the impeachment memorial; at the time the Prince of Ancheng stood attending on the hall steps, looked up at Emperor Wen, sweat streaming and countenance changed; Ling sent a palace attendant to escort the prince down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling stepped forward and read the impeachment memorial. The Prince of Ancheng, standing in attendance on the hall steps, looked up at Emperor Wen with sweat streaming down his face and his color gone. Ling sent a palace attendant to escort the prince from the hall.

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: From this the court was respectfully subdued.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the court was subdued with respect.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，領大著作。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Personnel Section, concurrently heading the Grand Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of personnel and concurrently headed the imperial historiography office.

sentences.zh: 陵以梁末以來，選授多失其所，於是提舉綱維，綜核名實。

translations.literal: Ling, because since the end of Liang appointments and grantings had often missed their proper place, thereupon raised up the governing standards and comprehensively verified names against reality.
translations.idiomatic: Because since the fall of Liang many appointments had gone to unworthy men, Xu Ling tightened the governing standards of selection and rigorously matched names to actual merit.

sentences.zh: 時有冒進求官，馳競不已者，乃為書宣示之，曰：「永定之時，聖朝草創，干戈未息，尚無條序。

translations.literal: At the time there were those who recklessly pushed forward seeking office, racing in competition without cease; he therefore composed a letter and displayed it to them, saying: 'In the time of Yongding, the holy dynasty was in the first founding, warfare had not ceased, and there was as yet no order and sequence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many men were recklessly scrambling for office without cease, so he circulated a letter of explanation, saying: 'In the Yongding era, when the dynasty was first being founded and warfare had not yet ceased, there was as yet no proper order to appointments.

sentences.zh: 府庫空虛，賞賜懸乏，白銀難得，黃劄易營。

translations.literal: The treasuries were empty and void, rewards and gifts were scarce and lacking, white silver was hard to obtain, and yellow appointment slips were easy to arrange.
translations.idiomatic: The treasuries were empty and rewards scarce. Silver was hard to come by, but yellow appointment documents were easy to issue.

sentences.zh: 權以官階，代于錢絹，義在撫接，無計多少。

translations.literal: Provisionally they used official ranks in place of cash and silk—the purpose lay in comforting and connecting, without reckoning how much.
translations.idiomatic: Official rank was used provisionally in place of cash and silk. The aim was to reassure and reward men, without counting the cost.

sentences.zh: 致令員外常侍，路上比肩，諮議參軍，市中無數，豈是朝章應其如此。

translations.literal: This caused supernumerary regular attendants to be shoulder to shoulder on the roads and advisory staff officers to be countless in the market—could court regulations rightly be thus?
translations.idiomatic: The result was supernumerary attendants crowding the roads shoulder to shoulder and advisory staff officers beyond count in the markets. Surely court regulations were never meant to produce this.

sentences.zh: 今衣冠禮樂，日富年華，何可猶作舊意，非理望也。

translations.literal: Now that cap-and-gown ritual and music grow richer day by day and the years flourish, how can one still act with the old intent? This is not reasonable expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Now that ritual and culture grow richer with each passing year, how can one still cling to the old ways? Such expectations are unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 所見諸君多踰本分，猶言大屈，未諭高懷。

translations.literal: Those I have seen mostly exceed their proper allotment, yet still say they suffer great wrong—I do not comprehend such lofty attitudes.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those I have seen already exceed their proper rank, yet still complain of great injustice. I cannot fathom such lofty expectations.

sentences.zh: 若問梁朝朱領軍異亦為卿相，此不踰其本分耶？

translations.literal: If you ask whether Zhu the Commander-in-Chief Yi of Liang also became a minister and chancellor—did he not exceed his proper allotment?
translations.idiomatic: If you ask whether Zhu Yi, commander-in-chief of Liang, also rose to minister and chancellor—did he not exceed his proper rank as well?

sentences.zh: 此是天子所拔，非關選序。

translations.literal: This was elevation by the Son of Heaven—it has nothing to do with the selection order.
translations.idiomatic: That was the emperor's personal elevation and had nothing to do with the normal selection process.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝云：'世間人言有目色，我特不目色範悌。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang said: 'People in the world say one has an eye for talent—I especially did not cast my eye on Fan Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang said, 'People say I have an eye for talent, but I deliberately did not cast my eye on Fan Ti.'

sentences.zh: '宋文帝亦云：'人豈無運命，每有好官缺，輒憶羊玄保。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song also said: 'Can a person truly be without fate? Whenever there was a good office vacant, I would always think of Yang Xuanbao.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song also said, 'Can a man truly be without fate? Whenever a good office fell vacant, I would always think of Yang Xuanbao.'

sentences.zh: '此則清階顯職，不由選也。

translations.literal: These were then exalted ranks and prominent offices—not obtained through selection.
translations.idiomatic: Such exalted and prominent offices are not obtained through the normal selection process.'

sentences.zh: 既忝衡流，諸賢深明鄙意。

translations.literal: Having been undeservedly placed at the helm of the stream, I trust you gentlemen deeply understand my humble intent.
translations.idiomatic: Having been undeservedly placed at the helm of personnel selection, I trust you gentlemen will understand my intent.

sentences.zh: 」自是眾咸服焉。

translations.literal: From this all submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: From that point all submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 時論比之毛玠。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion compared him to Mao Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion compared him to Mao Jie.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝入輔，謀黜異志者，引陵預其議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent, in plotting to remove those of heterodox intent, they brought in Ling to participate in the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan entered as regent and plotted to remove those of disloyal intent, Xu Ling was brought in to participate in the deliberations.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，封建昌縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changchang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he enfeoffed Xu Ling as Marquis of Changchang County.

sentences.zh: 太建中，為尚書左僕射，抗表推周弘正、王勱等。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era, he served as Left Vice Director of the Ministry of the Interior, and in a memorial resisted the appointment and recommended Zhou Hongzheng, Wang Mai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian era he served as left vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, but submitted a memorial declining the post and recommending Zhou Hongzheng, Wang Mai, and others instead.

sentences.zh: 帝召入內殿，曰：「卿何為固辭而舉人乎？

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him into the inner hall and said: 'Why do you firmly decline yet recommend others?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to the inner hall and said, 'Why do you firmly decline the post yourself yet recommend others?'

sentences.zh: 」陵曰：「弘正舊蕃長史，王勱太平中相府長史，張種帝鄉賢戚，若選賢舊，臣宜居後。

translations.literal: Ling said: 'Hongzheng was once chief administrator of my old frontier commandery, Mai was chief administrator of the chancellor's office in the Taiping era, and Zhang Zhong is a worthy kinsman from the emperor's native district—if one selects men of talent and standing, I ought to come after them.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling replied, 'Zhou Hongzheng was once chief administrator of my old commandery, Wang Mai was chief administrator of the chancellor's office during the Taiping era, and Zhang Zhong is a worthy kinsman from Your Majesty's home district. If merit and seniority are the standard, I ought to come after them.'

sentences.zh: 」固辭累日，乃奉詔。

translations.literal: He firmly declined for many days, then at last accepted the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He declined firmly for many days before at last accepting the edict.

sentences.zh: 及朝議北侵，宣帝命舉元帥，眾議在淳於量，陵獨曰：「不然。

translations.literal: When the court deliberated on a northern invasion, Emperor Xuan ordered nomination of a commander-in-chief; the assembly's opinion favored Chunyu Liang, but Ling alone said: 'Not so.
translations.idiomatic: When the court deliberated a northern campaign, Emperor Xuan ordered nominations for a commander-in-chief. The assembly favored Chunyu Liang, but Xu Ling alone said, 'Not so.'

sentences.zh: 吳明徹家在淮左，悉彼風俗，將略人才，當今無過者。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche's family is on the left bank of the Huai; he fully knows their customs and ways, and in military talent and capacity there is today none his superior.'
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche's family is from the Huai region and he knows its customs thoroughly. In military talent there is today no one his superior.'

sentences.zh: 」於是爭論數日不能決，都官尚書裴忌曰：「臣同徐僕射。

translations.literal: Thereupon they argued for several days without reaching a decision; Minister of Capital Affairs Pei Ji said: 'I agree with Vice Director Xu.'
translations.idiomatic: The debate continued for several days without resolution. Minister Pei Ji said, 'I agree with Vice Director Xu.'

sentences.zh: 」陵應聲曰：「非但明徹良將，忌即良副也。

translations.literal: Ling answered on the spot: 'Not only is Mingche an excellent general—Ji himself is an excellent deputy.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling answered at once, 'Not only is Mingche an excellent general—Ji himself would make an excellent deputy.'

sentences.zh: 」是日詔明徹為大都督，令忌監軍事，遂克淮南數十州地。

translations.literal: That day an edict made Mingche Grand Commander-in-Chief and ordered Ji to oversee military affairs; they thereupon captured several dozen prefectures of the Huainan region.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict appointed Wu Mingche grand commander-in-chief and ordered Pei Ji to oversee military affairs. They went on to capture dozens of prefectures in the Huainan region.

sentences.zh: 宣帝因置酒，舉杯屬陵曰：「賞卿知人。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan thereupon set out wine, raised his cup and entrusted it to Ling, saying: 'I reward you for knowing men.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan then held a banquet, raised his cup toward Xu Ling, and said, 'This toast rewards your eye for talent.'

sentences.zh: 七年，領國子祭酒，以公事免侍中、僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he headed the Directorate of the National University; because of official business he was relieved of the posts of Palace Attendant and Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he headed the imperial university, and was relieved of his posts as palace attendant and vice director on account of official duties.

sentences.zh: 尋加侍中，給扶。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Palace Attendant and granted a support staff.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again made palace attendant and granted attendants to support him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，為中書監，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he became Director of the Central Secretariat, concurrently Superintendent of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became director of the Secretariat and concurrently superintendent of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 以年老累表求致事，宣帝亦優禮之，詔將作為造大齋，令陵就第攝事。

translations.literal: Because of old age he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; Emperor Xuan also treated him with special honor, edicting the Directorate of Construction to build a great study and ordering Ling to handle affairs from his residence.
translations.idiomatic: As he aged he repeatedly memorialized to request retirement. Emperor Xuan treated him with special honor, ordering the directorate of construction to build a great study at his residence and allowing him to conduct affairs from home.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，遷左光祿大夫、太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord took the throne, he was transferred to Left Grand Master for Distinguished Service and Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord took the throne, Xu Ling was transferred to left grand master for distinguished service and junior tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 至德元年卒，年七十七，詔贈特進。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he died, at age seventy-seven; an edict posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhide at the age of seventy-seven, and an edict posthumously granted him the title of grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 初，後主為文示陵，雲他人所作。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Later Lord showed a literary composition to Ling, claiming it was someone else's work.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Later Lord showed Xu Ling a piece of writing and claimed it was someone else's composition.

sentences.zh: 陵嗤之曰：「都不成辭句。

translations.literal: Ling scoffed and said: 'It doesn't even form proper phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling scoffed and said, 'This doesn't even form proper sentences.'

sentences.zh: 」後主銜之，至是諡曰章偽侯。

translations.literal: The Later Lord harbored resentment; at this time his posthumous title was given as Marquis of Fraudulent Composition.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord harbored a grudge, and at this time gave him the posthumous title Marquis of Fraudulent Composition.

sentences.zh: 陵器局深遠，容止可觀，性又清簡，無所營樹，俸祿與親族共之。

translations.literal: Ling's capacity and bearing were deep and far-reaching, his deportment and appearance admirable; his nature was also pure and sparing—he made no arrangements for profit, and shared his salary and emoluments with kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling's breadth of character was profound, his bearing admirable, and his nature pure and spare. He sought no personal gain and shared his salary with his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 太建中，食建昌戶，戶送米至水次，親戚有貧匱者，皆召令取焉，數日便盡。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era, he drew sustenance from the households of Changchang; when the households delivered rice to the waterfront, those among his relatives who were poor and destitute were all summoned to take it—within a few days it was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taijian era he drew income from the households of his Changchang fief. When the households delivered rice to the waterfront, he summoned impoverished relatives to take what they needed, and within a few days it was all gone.

sentences.zh: 陵家尋致乏絕。

translations.literal: Ling's household soon came to want and deprivation.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling's household soon fell into want.

sentences.zh: 府僚怪問其故，陵云：「我有車牛衣裳可賣，餘家有可賣不？

translations.literal: The staff officials wondered and asked the reason; Ling said: 'I have carts, oxen, and clothes that can be sold—do you others at home have anything that can be sold?'
translations.idiomatic: His staff officials wondered and asked why. Xu Ling said, 'I still have carts, oxen, and clothes that can be sold. Do any of you at home have anything worth selling?'

sentences.zh: 」其周給如此。

translations.literal: Such was his exhaustive giving to others.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the extent of his generosity to others.

sentences.zh: 少而崇信釋教，經論多所釋解。

translations.literal: From youth he reverently believed in the Buddhist teaching and had explanatory interpretations of many sutras and treatises.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he devoutly embraced Buddhism and wrote interpretive commentaries on many sutras and treatises.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，令陵講大品經，義學名僧，自遠雲集，每講筵商較，四坐莫能與抗。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord was in the Eastern Palace, he had Ling lecture on the Mahaprajnaparamita Sutra; eminent monks of doctrinal learning gathered like clouds from afar, and at each lecture session when they debated, none in the four quarters could match him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord was crown prince, he had Xu Ling lecture on the Perfection of Wisdom Sutra. Eminent monks of doctrinal learning gathered from afar, and at each lecture session none among the assembled could hold their own against him in debate.

sentences.zh: 目有青精，時人以為聰慧之相也。

translations.literal: His eyes had a bluish gleam—people of the time took it as a sign of keen intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes had a bluish gleam, which people of the time regarded as a mark of keen intelligence.

sentences.zh: 自陳創業，文檄軍書及受禪詔策，皆陵所制，為一代文宗。

translations.literal: From Chen's founding, proclamations, military dispatches, and the abdication edicts and accession plans were all composed by Ling; he was the literary patriarch of an age.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of Chen, all proclamations, military dispatches, and abdication and accession documents were composed by Xu Ling, who became the literary patriarch of his generation.

sentences.zh: 亦不以矜物，未嘗詆訶作者。

translations.literal: Yet he did not use this to condescend to others, and never disparaged other writers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never used his stature to condescend to others, and never disparaged other writers.

sentences.zh: 其於後進，接引無倦。

translations.literal: Toward those coming after him, he guided and received them without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Toward younger writers he offered guidance and encouragement without weariness.

sentences.zh: 文、宣之時，國家有大手筆，必命陵草之。

translations.literal: In the times of Wen and Xuan, whenever the state had a major composition, Ling was invariably ordered to draft it.
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Emperors Wen and Xuan, whenever the state required a major composition, Xu Ling was invariably ordered to draft it.

sentences.zh: 其文頗變舊體，緝裁巧密，多有新意。

translations.literal: His writing considerably altered the old style—its assembly and pruning were artful and precise, and it often had fresh ideas.
translations.idiomatic: His writing markedly transformed the old style: its structure was artful and precise, and it often contained fresh ideas.

sentences.zh: 每一文出，好事者已傳寫成誦，遂傳于周、齊，家有其本。

translations.literal: Each time a composition issued, enthusiasts would already copy and recite it; it then spread to Zhou and Qi, and every household had its text.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a new piece appeared, enthusiasts would already copy and memorize it. His works spread to Northern Zhou and Northern Qi, and households everywhere kept copies.

sentences.zh: 後逢喪亂，多散失，存者三十卷。

translations.literal: Later they encountered turmoil and disorder, and most were scattered and lost; thirty scrolls survive.
translations.idiomatic: Later, amid the chaos of war, most were scattered and lost. Thirty scrolls survive.

sentences.zh: 陵有四子：儉、份、儀、僔。

translations.literal: Ling had four sons: Jian, Fen, Yi, and Tun.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling had four sons: Jian, Fen, Yi, and Tun.

sentences.zh: 儉一名報，幼而修立，勤學有志操。

translations.literal: Jian, also named Bao, from youth cultivated upright conduct, studied diligently, and had resolute integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Jian, also called Bao, cultivated upright conduct from youth, studied diligently, and possessed resolute integrity.

sentences.zh: 汝南周弘直重其為人，妻之以女。

translations.literal: Zhou Hongzhi of Runan esteemed his character and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Hongzhi of Runan admired his character and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝召為尚書金部郎中。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang summoned him as Lang of the Gold Section of the Ministry of the Interior.
