translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang summoned him to serve as director of the Ministry's gold section.

sentences.zh: 常侍宴賦詩，元帝歎賞之，曰：「徐氏之子，復有文矣。

translations.literal: He often attended banquets and composed poetry; Emperor Yuan sighed in admiration and said: 'The Xu family again has a man of letters.'
translations.idiomatic: He often attended banquets and composed poetry on command. Emperor Yuan sighed in admiration and said, 'The Xu family again has a man of letters.'

sentences.zh: 」魏平江陵，還建鄴，累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jiangling, he returned to Jiankang and was gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei forces captured Jiangling, he returned to Jiankang and was gradually promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太建初，廣州刺史歐陽紇舉兵反，宣帝令儉持節喻旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian, Ouyang He, Governor of Guangzhou, raised troops in rebellion; Emperor Xuan ordered Jian to bear the staff of office and proclaim the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taijian era, Ouyang He, governor of Guangzhou, raised troops in rebellion. Emperor Xuan ordered Xu Jian to bear the staff of office and convey the imperial message.

sentences.zh: 紇見儉，盛列仗衛，言辭不恭。

translations.literal: He, upon seeing Jian, arrayed his guards in full display, and his words were disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang He received Xu Jian, he displayed his guards in full array and spoke disrespectfully.

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「呂嘉之事，誠當已遠，將軍獨不見周迪、陳寶應乎？

translations.literal: Jian said: 'The affair of Lü Jia indeed must be far in the past—but does the general alone not see what became of Zhou Di and Chen Baoying?'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian said, 'The affair of Lü Jia may indeed be long ago—but has the general alone not seen what became of Zhou Di and Chen Baoying?'

sentences.zh: 」紇默然不答。

translations.literal: He fell silent and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang He fell silent and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 懼儉沮眾，不許入城，置儉於孤園寺。

translations.literal: Fearing Jian would discourage the troops, he would not permit him to enter the city and placed Jian at Guguan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Xu Jian would demoralize his troops, he refused to let him enter the city and confined him at Guguan Temple.

sentences.zh: 紇嘗出見儉，儉謂曰：「將軍業已舉事，儉須還報天子。

translations.literal: When He once came out to see Jian, Jian said to him: 'The general has already raised the affair—Jian must return to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Ouyang He once came out to see him, Xu Jian said, 'The general has already raised the banner of rebellion. I must return to report to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 儉之性命雖在將軍，將軍成敗不在於儉。

translations.literal: Jian's life though rests with the general, the general's success or failure does not depend on Jian.
translations.idiomatic: My life may rest in the general's hands, but the general's success or failure does not depend on me.

sentences.zh: 幸不見留。

translations.literal: I hope you will not detain me.'
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will not detain me.'

sentences.zh: 」紇於是遣儉。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent Jian away.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang He thereupon sent Xu Jian on his way.

sentences.zh: 從間道馳還。

translations.literal: He raced back by a hidden path.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian raced back by a hidden route.

sentences.zh: 宣帝乃命章昭達討紇，以儉監昭達軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan then ordered Zhang Zhaoda to attack He, with Jian supervising Zhao's army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan then ordered Zhang Zhaoda to campaign against Ouyang He, with Xu Jian supervising Zhang's army.

sentences.zh: 紇平，為兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: When He was pacified, Jian was appointed Concurrent Master of Ceremonies Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Ouyang He was defeated, Xu Jian was appointed concurrent master of ceremonies attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後主立，累遷尋陽內史，為政嚴明，盜賊靜息。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord was established, Jian was gradually promoted to Governor of Xunyang; his governance was strict and clear, and bandits and robbers subsided.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord took the throne, Xu Jian was gradually promoted to governor of Xunyang. His administration was strict and clear, and banditry subsided.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，襲封建昌侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Fast Cavalry and inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Changchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regular attendant of the fast cavalry and inherited the title of Marquis of Changchang.

sentences.zh: 入為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 儉公平無所阿附，尚書令江總望重一時，為儉所劾，後主深委任焉。

translations.literal: Jian was fair and attached himself to no faction; Jiang Zong, Director of the Ministry of the Interior, whose prestige weighed heavily in the age, was impeached by Jian, and the Later Lord deeply trusted and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian was fair and attached himself to no faction. Even Jiang Zong, director of the Ministry of Personnel and the most influential man of his day, was impeached by Jian. The Later Lord deeply trusted and relied on him.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Zhenming.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhenming.

sentences.zh: 份少有父風。

translations.literal: Fen from youth had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Fen from youth showed his father's character.

sentences.zh: 九歲為夢賦，陵見之，謂所親曰：「吾幼屬文亦不加此。

translations.literal: At nine he wrote a Dream Rhapsody; Ling saw it and told those close to him: 'When I was young and composed literature, I did not surpass this.'
translations.idiomatic: At nine he wrote a Dream Rhapsody. When Xu Ling saw it, he told those close to him, 'When I was young and wrote, I did not surpass this.'

sentences.zh: 」為海鹽令，有政績。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Haiyan and had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Haiyan and achieved a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 入為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Groom of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as groom of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 性孝弟，陵嘗疾篤，份燒香泣涕，跪誦孝經，日夜不息，如是者三日，陵疾豁然而愈，親戚皆謂份孝感所致。

translations.literal: His nature was filial and brotherly; Ling once fell gravely ill, and Fen burned incense and wept tears, knelt reciting the Classic of Filial Piety without ceasing day and night; after three days thus, Ling's illness suddenly cleared and he recovered—relatives all said it was caused by Fen's filial response.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial and dutiful toward his brothers. When Xu Ling once fell gravely ill, Fen burned incense and wept, kneeling to recite the Classic of Filial Piety day and night without cease. After three days of this, Ling's illness suddenly lifted and he recovered. Relatives all attributed it to Fen's filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 先陵卒。

translations.literal: Ling died first.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling died first.

sentences.zh: 儀少聰警，仕陳位尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: Yi from youth was clever and alert; serving Chen, he held the post of Secretariat Gentleman in the Ministry of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yi was bright and quick-witted from youth. Under Chen he served as a secretariat gentleman in the ministry of the interior.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，隱于錢唐之赭山。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he retired and hid on Mount Zhe in Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he withdrew into seclusion on Mount Zhe in Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝召為學士，尋除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui summoned him as an academician; soon he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Director of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui summoned him as a court academician and soon appointed him assistant director in the directorate of compilation.

sentences.zh: 大業四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 陵弟孝克，有口辯，能談玄理。

translations.literal: Ling's younger brother Kecheng had eloquent speech and could discuss dark principles.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling's younger brother Kecheng was a gifted speaker and could discourse on metaphysical doctrine.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，遭父憂殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: His nature was utterly filial; on encountering his father's death he nearly could not bear the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was profoundly filial by nature. When his father died, he nearly succumbed to grief.

sentences.zh: 事所生母陳氏，盡就養之道。

translations.literal: He served his biological mother, Lady Chen, fully fulfilling the way of supporting parents.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his biological mother, Lady Chen, and fully observed every duty of supporting a parent.

sentences.zh: 梁末，侯景寇亂，孝克養母，饘粥不能給。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, Hou Jing raided and brought disorder; Kecheng supported his mother, but gruel could not be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Liang, when Hou Jing's raids plunged the realm into chaos, Kecheng struggled to support his mother and could not even keep her supplied with gruel.

sentences.zh: 妻東莞臧氏，領軍將軍盾女也，甚有容色。

translations.literal: His wife was of the Zang clan of Dongguan, daughter of General-in-Chief Zang Dun, and was very beautiful in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Lady Zang of Dongguan, daughter of General-in-Chief Zang Dun, and was strikingly beautiful.

sentences.zh: 孝克乃謂曰：「今饑荒如此，供養交闕，欲嫁卿與富人，望彼此俱濟，於卿如何？

translations.literal: Kecheng thereupon said to her: 'Now famine is like this, support mutually lacking; I wish to marry you off to a rich man, hoping that both sides may be helped—what do you think?'
translations.idiomatic: Kecheng then said to her, "Famine is so severe that I can no longer provide for you. I want to marry you to a wealthy man, hoping we may both survive. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」臧氏弗許之。

translations.literal: Lady Zang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zang refused.

sentences.zh: 時有孔景行者，為侯景將，多從左右逼而迎之，臧氏涕泣而去，所得穀帛，悉以遺母。

translations.literal: At the time there was Kong Jingxing, a general of Hou Jing; with many followers he pressed and took her in marriage. Lady Zang wept as she departed; the grain and cloth she obtained she entirely sent to her mother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Kong Jingxing, a general under Hou Jing, came with a large retinue and forced her into marriage. Lady Zang left in tears, but sent all the grain and cloth she received to Kecheng's mother.

sentences.zh: 孝克又剃髮為沙門，改名法整，兼乞食以充給焉。

translations.literal: Kecheng again shaved his head and became a monk, changing his name to Fazheng, and also begged for food to fill their needs.
translations.idiomatic: Kecheng then shaved his head and became a monk, taking the religious name Fazheng, and also begged for alms to make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 臧氏亦深念舊恩，數私致饋餉，故不乏絕。

translations.literal: Lady Zang also deeply remembered their old bond and repeatedly sent provisions in secret, so they did not run out.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zang still cherished their old bond and secretly sent provisions many times, so they never entirely went without.

sentences.zh: 後景行戰死，臧氏伺孝克於途中，累日乃見，謂孝克曰：「往日之事，非為相負，今既得脫，當歸供養。

translations.literal: Later Jingxing died in battle; Lady Zang waited for Kecheng on the road and after several days finally saw him. She said to Kecheng: 'What happened in the past was not because I betrayed you. Now that I am free, I should return to support you.'
translations.idiomatic: Later Jingxing died in battle. Lady Zang waited for Kecheng on the road and, after several days, finally met him. She said, "What happened before was not because I meant to betray you. Now that I am free, I should come back and care for you."

sentences.zh: 」孝克默然無答。

translations.literal: Kecheng was silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Kecheng said nothing.

sentences.zh: 於是歸俗，更為夫妻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to lay life and again became husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to lay life, and they became husband and wife once more.

sentences.zh: 後東游，居錢唐之佳義裏，與諸僧討論釋典，遂通三論。

translations.literal: Later he traveled east and lived in Jiayi Lane in Qiantang, discussing Buddhist scriptures with the monks, and thereby mastered the Three Treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Later he traveled east and settled in Jiayi Lane in Qiantang, where he debated Buddhist scripture with the monks until he mastered the Three Treatises school.

sentences.zh: 每日二時講，旦講佛經，晚講禮傳，道俗受業者數百人。

translations.literal: Each day he lectured at two sessions: in the morning on Buddhist sutras, in the evening on the Rites and Commentary; clerics and laymen receiving instruction numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he lectured twice—on Buddhist sutras in the morning and on the Rites and Commentary in the evening—and several hundred clerics and lay disciples studied under him.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，除剡令，非其好，尋去職。

translations.literal: During Tianjia he was appointed magistrate of Shan; it was not to his liking, and he soon left office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjia era he was appointed magistrate of Shan, but the post did not suit him and he soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，徵為秘書丞，不就。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was summoned as Assistant Director of the Secretariat, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Taijian era he was summoned to serve as assistant director of the secretariat, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 乃蔬食長齋，持菩薩戒，晝夜講誦法華經。

translations.literal: He then ate vegetables and kept a long fast, observed the bodhisattva precepts, and day and night lectured on and recited the Lotus Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on vegetables, kept long fasts, observed the bodhisattva precepts, and lectured on and recited the Lotus Sutra day and night.

sentences.zh: 宣帝甚嘉其操行。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan greatly praised his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan greatly admired his character.

sentences.zh: 後為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he became Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He later became director of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 孝克每侍宴，無所食噉，至席散，當其前膳羞損減。

translations.literal: Whenever Kecheng attended banquets he ate nothing; when the feast ended, the delicacies before him were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kecheng attended banquets he ate nothing, yet when the feast ended the delicacies set before him were noticeably diminished.

sentences.zh: 帝密記以問中書舍人管斌，斌自是伺之，見孝克取珍果納紳帶中。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly noted this and asked Secretariat Gentleman Guan Bin; from then on Bin watched him and saw Kecheng take precious fruits and put them in his sash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took note of this and quietly asked Secretariat Gentleman Guan Bin about it. Bin then watched him and saw Kecheng slip choice fruits into his sash.

sentences.zh: 斌當時莫識其意，後尋訪，方知其以遺母。

translations.literal: At the time Bin did not understand his meaning; later, on inquiry, he finally learned that it was to send them to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Bin did not understand what he was doing. Only later, after making inquiries, did he learn that Kecheng was taking the food home to his mother.

sentences.zh: 斌以啟，宣帝嗟歎良久，乃敕自今宴享，孝克前饌，並遣將還，以餉其母。

translations.literal: Bin reported this; Emperor Xuan sighed in admiration for a long while and then ordered that from then on, at banquets and feasts, the food set before Kecheng should all be sent back to feed his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Bin reported what he had seen. Emperor Xuan sighed in admiration for a long while and then ordered that from then on, at every banquet, the food placed before Kecheng should be sent home to feed his mother.

sentences.zh: 時論美之。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised the emperor's kindness.

sentences.zh: 孝克性清素，好施惠，故不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Kecheng's nature was pure and simple; he loved to give generously, and so could not avoid hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Kecheng lived plainly and loved to give to others, and so never escaped poverty.

sentences.zh: 後主敕以石頭津稅給之，孝克悉用設齋寫經，隨盡。

translations.literal: The Later Lord ordered that the Shitou ferry tax be given to him; Kecheng used it all for vegetarian feasts and copying sutras, spending it as fast as it came.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord ordered that the ferry tax at Shitou be paid to him, but Kecheng spent it all on vegetarian feasts and copying sutras as soon as it arrived.

sentences.zh: 二年，為散騎常侍，侍東宮。

translations.literal: In the second year he became Regular Attendant and attended the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed regular attendant and attended the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，隨例入長安。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, following convention he entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he went to Chang'an along with the other former officials.

sentences.zh: 家道壁立，所生母患，欲粳米為粥，不能常辦。

translations.literal: His household was destitute; his biological mother fell ill and wished for polished rice made into gruel, but he could not regularly provide it.
translations.idiomatic: His household was utterly destitute. His biological mother fell ill and wanted gruel made from polished rice, but he could not provide it regularly.

sentences.zh: 母亡後，孝克遂常噉麥，有遺粳米者，孝克對而悲泣，終身不復食焉。

translations.literal: After his mother died, Kecheng then regularly ate wheat; when someone gave him polished rice, Kecheng faced it and wept in grief, and for the rest of his life never ate it again.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, Kecheng lived mainly on wheat. If anyone gave him polished rice, he would look at it and weep, and he never ate it again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 開皇十二年，長安疾疫，隋文帝聞其名行，召令于尚書都堂講金剛般若經。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaihuang, when plague struck Chang'an, Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his reputation and conduct and summoned him to lecture on the Diamond Prajna Sutra in the main hall of the Ministry of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Kaihuang era, when plague swept Chang'an, Emperor Wen of Sui heard of his reputation and summoned him to lecture on the Diamond Prajna Sutra in the main hall of the ministry of the interior.

sentences.zh: 尋授國子博士，後侍東宮，講禮傳。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Doctor of the National University; later he attended the Eastern Palace and lectured on the Rites and Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed a doctor of the national university, and later attended the eastern palace, where he lectured on the Rites and Commentary.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以疾卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died of illness, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he died of illness at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 臨終政坐念佛，室內有非常香氣，鄰里皆驚異之。

translations.literal: At the approach of death he sat upright reciting the Buddha's name; within the room there was an extraordinary fragrance, and neighbors were all astonished.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached he sat upright reciting the Buddha's name. An extraordinary fragrance filled the room, and all the neighbors were astonished.

sentences.zh: 子萬載，位太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His son Wanzai held the post of Groom of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wanzai served as groom of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 鮑泉字潤嶽，東海人也。

translations.literal: Bao Quan, styled Runyue, was a man of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Quan, courtesy name Runyue, came from Donghai.

sentences.zh: 父幾字景玄，家貧，以母老詣吏部尚書王亮幹祿，亮一見嗟賞，舉為舂陵令。

translations.literal: His father Ji, styled Jingxuan, was poor; because his mother was old he went to Minister of the Interior Wang Liang to seek a salary post; Liang sighed in admiration at first sight and recommended him as magistrate of Chunling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bao Ji, styled Jingxuan, was poor. With an aged mother to support, he went to Minister Wang Liang to seek an appointment. Liang was impressed at once and had him named magistrate of Chunling.

sentences.zh: 後為明山賓所薦，為太常丞。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended by Ming Shanbin and became Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on Ming Shanbin's recommendation, he became vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以外兄傅昭為太常，依制緦服不得相臨，改為尚書郎，終於湘東王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Because his cousin by marriage Fu Zhao became Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, by regulation those in mourning dress of the second degree could not supervise one another, so he was changed to a Lang of the Ministry of the Interior and ended as advisory staff member to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When his cousin by marriage Fu Zhao became director of the court of imperial sacrifices, regulations forbade men in second-degree mourning from holding office under one another, so he was transferred to a post in the ministry of the interior and ended his career as an adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 泉美須髯，善舉止，身長八尺，性甚警悟。

translations.literal: Quan had a fine beard and moustache, graceful bearing, a height of eight chi, and a nature very quick and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: Quan had a handsome beard, graceful bearing, and stood eight chi tall. He was exceptionally quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 博涉史傳，兼有文筆。

translations.literal: He broadly studied histories and biographies and also possessed literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in history and biography and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 少事元帝為國常侍，早見擢任，謂曰：「我文之外無出卿者。

translations.literal: From youth he served Emperor Yuan as regular attendant of the state; he was early selected for promotion, and the emperor said to him: 'Apart from my own writing, none surpasses yours.'
translations.idiomatic: From youth he served Emperor Yuan as a regular attendant and was promoted early. The emperor told him, 'Apart from my own writing, no one surpasses you.'

sentences.zh: 」後為通直侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Attendant for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: He later became attendant for direct communication.

sentences.zh: 常乘高幰車，從數十左右，傘蓋服玩甚精。

translations.literal: He often rode in a high-canopied carriage with several dozen attendants; his parasols, canopies, clothing, and ornaments were very fine.
translations.idiomatic: He often traveled in a high-canopied carriage with dozens of attendants, his parasols, robes, and ornaments all of the finest sort.

sentences.zh: 道逢國子祭酒王承，承疑非舊貴，遣訪之，泉從者答曰：「鮑通直」。

translations.literal: On the road he met Director of the Imperial Academy Wang Cheng; Cheng suspected he was not old nobility and sent someone to inquire—Quan's follower answered: 'Attendant Bao.'
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met Wang Cheng, director of the imperial academy. Cheng doubted he was old aristocracy and sent someone to ask who he was. Quan's attendant replied, 'Attendant Bao.'

sentences.zh: 承怪焉，復欲辱之，遣逼車問：「鮑通直復是何許人，而得如此！

translations.literal: Cheng thought it strange and again wished to humiliate him, sending someone to press up to the carriage and ask: 'Attendant Bao—who in the world is he, to live like this!'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng found this odd and tried to humiliate him further, sending a man to press up to the carriage and demand, 'Who in the world is Attendant Bao, to live like this?'

sentences.zh: 」都下少年遂為口實，見尚豪華人，相戲曰：「鮑通直復是何許人，而得如此」，以為笑謔。

translations.literal: Youth in the capital then made it a byword; seeing someone fond of luxury, they would jest: 'Who in the world is Attendant Bao, to live like this?'—taking it as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: Capital youths turned the line into a catchphrase. Whenever they saw someone decked out in luxury, they would tease, 'Who in the world is Attendant Bao, to live like this?' and laugh.

sentences.zh: 及元帝承制，累遷至信州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan assumed government, Quan was progressively promoted to Inspector of Xin province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan assumed power, Quan rose through the ranks to inspector of Xin province.

sentences.zh: 方等之敗，元帝大怒，泉與王僧辯討之。

translations.literal: After Fangdeng's defeat, Emperor Yuan was greatly angry; Quan campaigned against the rebels with Wang Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: After Fangdeng's defeat the emperor was furious and sent Quan with Wang Sengbian to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 僧辯曰：「計將安出？

translations.literal: Sengbian said: 'What plan shall we adopt?'
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian asked, 'What is your plan?'

sentences.zh: 」泉曰：「事等沃雪，何所多慮。

translations.literal: Quan said: 'The affair is like pouring water on snow—why so much worry?'
translations.idiomatic: Quan said, 'This will melt away like snow under hot water. Why worry so much?'

sentences.zh: 」僧辯曰：「君言文士常談耳，河東少有武幹，非精兵一萬不可以往。

translations.literal: Sengbian said: 'Your words are the usual talk of literary men. Hedong has no small military talent—we cannot go without ten thousand picked troops.'
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian replied, 'That is the sort of thing literary men always say. Hedong is no pushover. We cannot go without ten thousand elite troops.'

sentences.zh: 竟陵甲卒不久當至，猶可重申。

translations.literal: The armored soldiers of Jingling will soon arrive—we can still restate the request.
translations.idiomatic: The armored troops from Jingling will arrive soon. We can still ask again then.

sentences.zh: 欲與卿入言之。

translations.literal: I wish to enter with you and speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: I want to go in with you and explain this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」泉許諾，及僧辯如向言，泉默然不繼。

translations.literal: Quan agreed; when Sengbian spoke as he had said, Quan fell silent and did not continue.
translations.idiomatic: Quan agreed, but when Sengbian made the argument as promised, Quan said nothing and did not back him up.

sentences.zh: 元帝大怒，於是械系僧辯，時人比泉為酈寄。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was greatly angry and had Sengbian shackled and imprisoned; people of the time compared Quan to Li Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and had Sengbian shackled and imprisoned. Contemporaries compared Quan to Li Ji, who had betrayed his friend.

sentences.zh: 泉既專征長沙，久而不克。

translations.literal: Quan, having sole command of the campaign against Changsha, long failed to capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Quan held sole command of the campaign against Changsha but could not take the city for a long time.

sentences.zh: 元帝乃數泉二十罪，為書責之曰：「面如冠玉，還疑木偶，須似蝟毛，徒勞繞喙。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan then listed twenty crimes against Quan and wrote to rebuke him, saying: 'Your face is like jade on a cap—one still suspects a wooden puppet; your beard is like hedgehog bristles—only in vain do you move your beak.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listed twenty crimes against Quan and wrote to rebuke him: 'Your face is like jade on a cap, yet one still suspects a wooden puppet. Your beard is like hedgehog bristles, yet all you do is flap your lips in vain.'

sentences.zh: 」乃從獄中起王僧辯代泉為都督，使舍人羅重歡領齋仗三百人與僧辯往。

translations.literal: He then raised Wang Sengbian from prison to replace Quan as commander-in-chief, and sent Gentleman Attendant Luo Chonghuan leading three hundred armed guards of the fast with Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: He then released Wang Sengbian from prison to replace Quan as commander and sent Gentleman Attendant Luo Chonghuan with three hundred armed guards to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 乃至長沙，遣通泉曰：「羅舍人被令送王竟陵來。

translations.literal: When they reached Changsha, he sent word to Quan: 'Gentleman Luo has been ordered to escort Wang of Jingling here.'
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Changsha he sent word to Quan: 'Gentleman Luo has been ordered to bring Wang of Jingling to assist you.'

sentences.zh: 」泉愕然，顧左右曰：「得王竟陵助我經略，賊不足平矣。

translations.literal: Quan was startled and, turning to those beside him, said: 'With Wang of Jingling to help me in strategy, the rebels are not worth crushing.'
translations.idiomatic: Quan was astonished and told his attendants, 'With Wang of Jingling to help me plan the campaign, the rebels will be nothing to crush.'

sentences.zh: 」乃拂席坐而待之。

translations.literal: He then brushed the mat and sat waiting for him.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed off a seat and sat waiting for him.

sentences.zh: 僧辯入，乃背泉而坐曰：「鮑郎，卿有罪，令旨使我鎖卿，卿勿以故意見期。

translations.literal: Sengbian entered, then sat with his back to Quan and said: 'Master Bao, you are guilty. By imperial order I am to fetter you—do not expect our old friendship.'
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian entered he sat with his back to Quan and said, 'Master Bao, you are guilty. By imperial order I am to fetter you. Do not count on our old friendship.'

sentences.zh: 」命重歡出令示泉，鎖之床下。

translations.literal: He ordered Chonghuan to produce the order and show it to Quan, and fettered him beside the bed.
translations.idiomatic: He had Chonghuan produce the order and show it to Quan, then shackled him beside the bed.

sentences.zh: 泉顏色自若，了無懼容，曰：「稽緩王師，罪乃甘分，但恐後人更思鮑泉之憒憒耳。

translations.literal: Quan's complexion was as before, with no sign of fear; he said: 'Delaying the imperial army—guilt I accept willingly. I only fear that later men will again think of Bao Quan's muddle.'
translations.idiomatic: Quan's color never changed and he showed no fear. He said, 'Delaying the imperial army is a guilt I accept. I only fear that later generations will remember Bao Quan's blundering.'

sentences.zh: 」僧辯色甚不平，泉乃啟陳淹遲之罪。

translations.literal: Sengbian looked very displeased; Quan then submitted a memorial stating the crime of delay.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian looked deeply offended. Quan then submitted a memorial confessing the crime of delay.

sentences.zh: 元帝尋復其任，令與僧辯等東逼邵陵王於郢州。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan soon restored his post and ordered him with Sengbian and others to press east against the Prince of Shaoling at Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon restored him to office and ordered him with Sengbian and others to march east and press the Prince of Shaoling at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 郢州平，元帝以世子方諸為刺史，泉為長史，行州府事。

translations.literal: When Ying province was pacified, Emperor Yuan made the heir Fangzhu inspector and Quan chief administrator, acting in charge of prefecture and headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Yingzhou was pacified, the emperor made the heir Fangzhu inspector and Quan chief administrator, with charge of the prefecture and headquarters.

sentences.zh: 方諸見泉和弱，每有諮陳未嘗用，使泉伏床騎背為馬，書其衣作其姓名，由是州府盡相欺。

translations.literal: Fangzhu, seeing Quan mild and weak, never used any advice he offered; he made Quan lie face down on a bed and rode his back as a horse, wrote on his clothes and made his name—whereupon the whole prefecture and headquarters joined in deceiving one another.
translations.idiomatic: Fangzhu found Quan mild and weak, never took his advice, made him lie on a bed and rode his back as a horse, and wrote his name on Quan's clothes. From then on everyone in the prefecture and headquarters joined in mocking him.

sentences.zh: 侯景密遣將宋子仙、任約襲之。

translations.literal: Hou Jing secretly sent generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing secretly sent his generals Song Zixian and Ren Yue to attack them.

sentences.zh: 方諸與泉不恤軍政，唯蒱酒自樂，云：「賊何由得至」。

translations.literal: Fangzhu and Quan did not attend to military affairs, only gambling and wine for their pleasure, saying: 'How could the enemy ever get here?'
translations.idiomatic: Fangzhu and Quan neglected military affairs and amused themselves with gambling and wine, saying, 'How could the enemy ever reach us here?'

sentences.zh: 既而傳告者眾，始命闔門。

translations.literal: Soon reports became numerous, and only then did they order the gates closed.
translations.idiomatic: When reports of the enemy multiplied, they finally ordered the gates shut.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊執方諸及泉送之景所。

translations.literal: The city fell; the rebels seized Fangzhu and Quan and sent them to Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. The rebels seized Fangzhu and Quan and sent them to Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 後景攻王僧辯于巴陵不克，敗還，乃殺泉于江夏，沈其屍于黃鶴磯。

translations.literal: Later Hou Jing attacked Wang Sengbian at Baling without success, returned in defeat, and then killed Quan at Jiangxia and sank his corpse at Yellow Crane Rock.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hou Jing attacked Wang Sengbian at Baling, failed, and retreated in defeat. He then executed Quan at Jiangxia and sank his body in the river at Yellow Crane Rock.

sentences.zh: 初，泉夢著朱衣行水上，及死，舉身帶血而沈于江如其夢。

translations.literal: Earlier Quan had dreamed of wearing red robes and walking on water; when he died, his whole body bloody, he was sunk in the river just as in the dream.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Quan had dreamed that he wore red robes and walked on water. When he died, his body covered in blood, he was sunk in the river exactly as in the dream.

sentences.zh: 泉于儀禮尤明，撰新儀三十卷行於世。

translations.literal: Quan was especially expert in ritual propriety and compiled New Rites in thirty scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was especially learned in ritual and compiled New Rites in thirty scrolls, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 時又有鮑行卿以博學大才稱，位後軍臨川王錄事，兼中書舍人，遷步兵校尉。

translations.literal: At the time there was also Bao Xingqing, famed for broad learning and great talent; he held the post of recorder to the Prince of Linchuan of the Rear Army, concurrently Secretariat Gentleman, and was transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was also Bao Xingqing, famed for erudition and literary talent. He served as recorder to the Prince of Linchuan of the rear army and as a concurrent secretariat gentleman, and was later promoted to commandant of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 上玉璧銘，武帝發詔褒賞。

translations.literal: He presented an inscription on a jade bi; Emperor Wu issued an edict praising and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: He presented an inscription on a jade bi, and Emperor Wu issued an edict praising and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 好韻語，及拜步兵，面謝帝曰：「作舍人，不免貧，得五校，實大校。

translations.literal: He loved witty rhymes; when appointed commandant of footsoldiers he thanked the emperor face to face, saying: 'As a Secretariat Gentleman, one cannot avoid being poor; obtaining the Five Commandants is truly a great commandant.'
translations.idiomatic: He loved witty rhymes. When he received appointment as commandant of footsoldiers, he thanked the emperor in person and said, "As a secretariat gentleman, one cannot avoid being poor; but gaining one of the Five Commandants is truly gaining a great commandant."

sentences.zh: 」例皆如此。

translations.literal: His examples were always like this.
translations.idiomatic: His remarks were always of this sort.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected writings in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 撰皇室儀十三卷，乘輿龍飛記二卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Imperial Household Rites in thirteen scrolls and Record of the Imperial Carriage's Dragon Ascent in two scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Imperial Household Rites in thirteen scrolls and Record of the Imperial Carriage's Dragon Ascent in two scrolls.

sentences.zh: 弟客卿位南康太守。

translations.literal: His younger brother Keqing held the post of Administrator of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Keqing served as administrator of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 客卿三子，檢、正、至，並才藝知名，俱為湘東王五佐。

translations.literal: Keqing's three sons, Jian, Zheng, and Zhi, were all famed for talent and accomplishment, and all served among the Prince of Xiangdong's five aides.
translations.idiomatic: Keqing's three sons—Jian, Zheng, and Zhi—were all known for talent and skill, and all served among the five aides of the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 正好交遊，無日不適人，人為之語曰：「無處不逢烏噪，無處不逢鮑佐。

translations.literal: Zheng loved socializing and never went a day without visiting someone; people made a saying of it: 'Nowhere without encountering crow caw, nowhere without encountering Bao the aide.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng loved company and never let a day pass without calling on someone. People said of him, "There is nowhere you won't hear crows cawing, and nowhere you won't run into Bao the aide."

sentences.zh: 」正不為湘東王所知，獻書告退。

translations.literal: Zheng was not appreciated by the Prince of Xiangdong and submitted a letter requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng failed to win the Prince of Xiangdong's favor and submitted a letter resigning his post.

sentences.zh: 王恨之。

translations.literal: The prince resented him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince resented him.

sentences.zh: 及建鄴城陷，正為尚書外兵郎，病不能起。

translations.literal: When Jiankang fell, Zheng was Outer Military Lang of the Ministry of the Interior and was too ill to rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Zheng was serving as outer military lang in the ministry of the interior, but he was too ill to rise.

sentences.zh: 景雜於死屍焚之。

translations.literal: Hou Jing mixed him among the dead corpses and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing threw him in among the dead and had the bodies burned.

sentences.zh: 王聞之曰：「忠非紀信，利非象齒，焚如棄如，於是乎得。

translations.literal: When the prince heard of it he said: 'His loyalty was not like Ji Xin's, his profit was not like ivory tusks—burned and cast away, and so it was done.'
translations.idiomatic: When the prince heard of it he said, "His loyalty was no Ji Xin's, his worth no ivory tusk—burn him and cast him aside, and there you have it."

sentences.zh: 」君子以此知湘東王不仁。

translations.literal: Gentlemen thereby knew that the Prince of Xiangdong was not humane.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment took this as proof that the Prince of Xiangdong lacked humanity.

sentences.zh: 檢為湘東鎮西府中記室，使蜀，不屈于武陵王，見害。

translations.literal: Jian was recording secretary in the Prince of Xiangdong's western headquarters; sent to Shu, he would not submit to the Prince of Wuzhou and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian served as recording secretary in the Prince of Xiangdong's western headquarters. Sent on a mission to Shu, he refused to submit to the Prince of Wuzhou and was killed.

sentences.zh: 論曰：夏侯勝雲，「士患不明經術，經術明，取青紫如拾地芥耳」。

translations.literal: The historian says: Xia Hou Sheng said, 'Scholars worry about not understanding the classics; when the classics are clear, obtaining purple and green rank is like picking mustard seeds from the ground.'
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Xia Hou Sheng said, "A scholar's trouble is not knowing the classics. Once the classics are mastered, winning office and rank is like picking mustard seeds off the ground."

sentences.zh: 于賀瑒、賀琛、朱異、司馬褧其得之矣。

translations.literal: He Yang, He Chen, Zhu Yi, and Sima Jiong obtained this.
translations.idiomatic: He Yang, He Chen, Zhu Yi, and Sima Jiong had done exactly that.

sentences.zh: 而異遂徼寵倖，任事居權，不能以道佐時，苟取容媚。

translations.literal: But Yi then sought favor and fortune, held office and wielded power, and could not assist the age by the Way, merely seeking to please and flatter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhu Yi went on to court favor and fortune, held office and wielded power, and instead of guiding the times by principle he sought only to please and flatter.

sentences.zh: 及延寇敗國，實異之由，禍難既彰，不明其罪，亦既身死，寵贈猶殊。

translations.literal: When he invited the bandits and ruined the state, it was truly because of Yi; though disaster was already manifest, his crime was not clarified; even after his death, honorific gifts were still exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: When he invited the invaders and brought the state to ruin, the blame truly lay with Zhu Yi. The catastrophe was plain for all to see, yet his guilt was never made clear; even after his death he received extraordinary posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 罰既弗加，賞亦斯濫。

translations.literal: Punishment was not applied, and reward was likewise excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment was never imposed, and reward was lavished just as recklessly.

sentences.zh: 夫太清之亂，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: The turmoil of Taqing—naturally it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The chaos of the Taqing era was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 顧協清介，足以追蹤古人，徐摛貞正，仁者信乎有勇。

translations.literal: Gu Xie was pure and upright, enough to follow in the tracks of the ancients; Xu Chi was upright and correct—the benevolent indeed have courage.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xie was pure and upright, worthy to be measured against the ancients. Xu Chi was steadfast and upright—the benevolent, it is said, also have courage.

sentences.zh: 孝穆聰明特達，締構興王，獻替謀猷，亮直斯在。

translations.literal: Xiao Mu was brilliant and exceptionally penetrating, established the rising king, offered counsel and strategy—candor was there.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling, styled Xiao Mu, was brilliant and far-seeing. He helped establish the rising dynasty, offered counsel in planning and policy, and his candor was always present.

sentences.zh: 泉本文房之士，每處荷戈之任，非材之責，勝任不亦難乎。

translations.literal: Quan was originally a man of the writing desk; each time placed in the duty of bearing arms—the blame for wrong talent—was fulfillment not also difficult?
translations.idiomatic: Bao Quan was a scholar of the writing desk by nature, yet time and again he was placed in command of troops. When the wrong man is given the wrong task, how can he be expected to succeed?
